input.title: Photo Production Assistant - Apparel
input.description: About Comfrt: Comfrt is one of the fastest-growing direct-to-consumer brands, dedicated to blending mental wellness, inclusivity, and elevated comfort into every piece we create. Our mission goes beyond clothing — we strive to build a community where everyone feels supported and seen. Role Overview: We are looking for a highly organized and detail-oriented Photo Production Assistant - Apparel to support the day-to-day operations of Comfrt's Miami studio. You will keep apparel samples organized and the studio running smoothly while providing hands-on support during photo production days—including setup, garment prep, and on-set logistics. This is an on-site role critical to ensuring our e-commerce and marketing photography goes off without a hitch. Key Responsibilities: Organize, catalog, and maintain inventory of all samples and production garments. Keep racks, shelves, and storage areas tidy, labeled, and logically organized at all times. Track all sample movement in and out of the studio for shoots, fittings, loans, and returns, ensuring accurate records are maintained. Perform quality control checks on garments prior to shoots, reviewing fit, construction, and cleanliness. Steam, tag, and prep all garments for content days and photo shoot days. Assist during fittings, photo shoots, and studio visits, including set-up, teardown, and on-set support throughout the day. Maintain overall studio cleanliness, including sweeping, tidying common areas, and managing supply levels. Proactively identify workflow improvements and stay ahead of studio needs before they become issues. Support miscellaneous errands, returns, and supply pickups as needed. Requirements: 2+ years of hands-on experience working in fashion/apparel photo production or photo studio environments, with proven experience supporting and prepping garments for photoshoots . Strong organizational and project management skills , with the ability to manage high-volume production workflows, timelines, and multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Experience with e-commerce, fashion, or apparel photography/production strongly preferred , with a professional understanding of studio and shoot processes. Exceptional organizational skills and a strong attention to detail. Experience with garment steaming, care, and quality inspection. Familiarity with sample tracking systems or inventory management tools. An eye for visual organization and brand presentation. Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously in a fast-paced environment without losing accuracy. A proactive, low-ego attitude. You take initiative, no task is too small, and you take pride in keeping things running smoothly. Strong communication skills and comfort working closely with a small, collaborative team. Physically able to stand for extended periods, lift garment racks, and handle the physical demands of an active studio environment. Based in Miami, FL . This role requires full-time, on-site presence. Must have own means of transportation Why Join Comfrt? Be part of a purpose-driven company that’s shaping the future of comfort and mental wellness. Work in a supportive, creative environment where your ideas and growth are valued. Enjoy Comfrt benefits such as generous paid time off, company-covered health insurance, 5% 401k match, and discounts on all Comfrt products! Comfrt is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.

input.title: Paid Media Manager
input.description: Join Telemundo’s Marketing team as a Paid Media Manager supporting integrated campaigns across entertainment, news, and sports. Reporting to the Paid Media Director, you will help turn approved media strategies into effective campaign execution across television, streaming, digital video, paid social, audio, and out-of-home channels. You will work closely with our media agency and internal partners to review media recommendations, coordinate campaign delivery, monitor performance, and identify opportunities to optimize results. You will also supervise a Paid Media Specialist. This is a temporary assignment covering a leave of absence. This is a project/limited term position, unless otherwise amended or terminated as deliverables within this project are completed. Key Responsibilities Review agency media recommendations and provide actionable feedback in partnership with the Paid Media Director and Audience Strategy team, as applicable. Work closely with the media agency to coordinate campaign implementation, track milestones, and support timely delivery across media channels. Partner with the Paid Media Director and Audience Strategy team, as applicable, to review key agency deliverables, including tactical plans, flowcharts, media authorizations, launch trackers, and campaign reports. Track campaign spending, pacing, flighting, and delivery against approved plans; identify discrepancies and escalate budget decisions or material risks to the Paid Media Director. Lead ongoing campaign performance analysis, assessing channel and creative results against relevant KPIs and benchmarks; recommend and coordinate optimizations subject to appropriate approvals. Review agency reporting, campaign wrap-ups, and measurement studies; synthesize actionable insights and learnings to inform future campaigns. Collaborate with Marketing Strategy, Creative, Social, and Operations on creative mapping, asset readiness, launch priorities, and integrated campaign updates. Oversee preparation and accuracy of paid media inputs for internal campaign decks, recaps, and cross-functional updates. Supervise and coach the Paid Media Specialist, setting priorities and overseeing quality, deadlines, and adherence to paid media procedures. Basic Requirements 5+ years of experience in paid media planning, activation, campaign management, or related roles at an agency or advertiser. Spanish-language proficiency is a must - Written and verbal Experience coordinating integrated paid media campaigns across digital and traditional channels. Strong analytical skills, including experience interpreting campaign reports, media KPIs, and optimization opportunities. Experience monitoring media budgets, pacing, campaign timelines, and execution deliverables. Proven ability to collaborate with external agencies and cross-functional stakeholders while managing competing deadlines. Experience supervising or providing day-to-day direction to junior team members. Strong written and verbal communication skills and proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint. Desired Characteristics Experience in entertainment, television, streaming, sports, or multicultural marketing. Familiarity with Meta, TikTok, YouTube, connected TV, and other digital advertising environments. Experience reviewing brand lift, attribution, or tune-in measurement studies. Ability to turn complex performance data into concise recommendations for business stakeholders. Strong organizational judgment, attention to detail, and comfort working in a fast-paced environment. input.title: Media Management Operations Specialist
input.description: This is a project/limited term position, unless otherwise amended or terminated as deliverables within this project are completed. The Media Management Operations Specialist is a specialized, hands-on technical role responsible for the processing, management, quality control, organization, storage, and lifecycle of media assets supporting network broadcast, sports, news, and production operations. Job Duties: Execute and monitor media ingest, transcoding, transfer, QC, archive, restoration, export, and distribution workflows across broadcast, post-production, and cloud-based environments. Manage and organize media within MAM, AVID, Cloud systems, archive, and shared-storage systems, ensuring assets are properly processed, organized, accessible, and available within required deadlines. Perform comprehensive technical and visual quality control (QC) of media, identifying issues involving video, audio, timecode, resolution, frame rate, synchronization, file integrity, metadata, and technical specifications. Validate metadata, naming conventions, folder structures, media placement, and delivery specifications to ensure accuracy and compliance with established standards. Monitor media storage, asset availability, retention, archive, and restoration activities in support of content lifecycle and storage-management requirements. Independently troubleshoot failed or delayed ingest, transcode, transfer, archive, restoration, and delivery workflows and perform appropriate first-level corrective actions. Analyze workflow failures, identify potential points of failure, gather relevant technical information, and provide detailed escalations to Engineering, Media Systems, and other technical teams when required. Support time-sensitive media requirements for live events, sports, digital streaming, broadcast, and production operations. Maintain accurate operational documentation and clearly communicate workflow status, technical discrepancies, risks, and escalations to appropriate stakeholders. Identify opportunities to improve media-management processes, operational efficiency, and workflow reliability. Collaborate with Media Operations, Sports Operations, Production, Editorial, Engineering, Media Systems, and other technical teams to resolve issues and meet critical production deadlines. Adapts to fluctuating schedules, including nights, overnights, weekends, and holidays, in a high-demand, fast-paced environment. Works under the direct supervision of the Sr Manager of Media Operations and is responsible for completing any other tasks as assigned by the manager. Basic Requirements: Minimum 5 years of experience in a production, postproduction, broadcast, or communications environment Fluency in English & Spanish Strong technical knowledge of broadcast media management and post-production workflows, including ingest, transcoding, QC, media movement, storage management, archive, restoration, distribution, and content lifecycle management. Demonstrated proficiency with professional MAM and AVID environments, including AVID Media Composer, Interplay, Media Central Cloud UX, Media Shuttle, or comparable broadcast and post-production platforms. Strong knowledge of professional video formats, codecs, resolutions, frame rates, and media specifications, including HD, UHD/4K, MXF, MOV, MP4, Apple ProRes, XAVC, and proxy media. Strong understanding of cloud-based broadcast and post-production environments, including Microsoft Azure or comparable cloud technologies and the integration of cloud and on-premises media workflows. Demonstrated expertise in technical and visual media QC, including the ability to identify and assess video, audio, timecode, synchronization, metadata, file-integrity, and specification-related issues. Strong knowledge of media storage, metadata management, naming conventions, folder structures, asset organization, retention, archive, and restoration principles. Demonstrated ability to independently troubleshoot media workflow failures, identify probable causes, perform initial corrective actions, and determine when technical escalation is required. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with an understanding of workflow dependencies and downstream impacts across editorial, production, distribution, and broadcast operations. Ability to interpret technical specifications and media delivery requirements and ensure assets meet established technical and operational standards. Ability to independently prioritize and manage multiple high-volume, time-sensitive workflows while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly communicate technical issues to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Ability to quickly learn and develop proficiency in new broadcast, post-production, MAM, cloud, and media-management technologies. Desired Characteristics: Bachelor’s or 2-year degree in Communications or Media preferred Experience in international broadcast operations or media. Familiarity with broadcast and digital streaming media workflows. input.description: About Chili Piper Chili Piper is a B2B SaaS company that helps GTM teams turn inbound leads into qualified meetings - instantly. We’re growing quickly and aiming big! ***CURRENTLY ONLY HIRING FOR THIS ROLE IN CANADA AND THE US*** About the role At Chili Piper, community and events are at the heart of our GTM strategy. From intimate dinners to large-scale activations like our annual ChiliPalooza, we bring top GTM leaders together to connect, exchange ideas, and build lasting relationships. It's how we turn a room full of people into real pipeline, and how we've built a community that actually wants to hear from us. We're hiring an Events Manager to scale these experiences and deepen our relationships with the GTM community: executive dinners, industry conferences, sponsorships, speaking moments, webinars, and ChiliPalooza. This is the person who turns our presence in a room, physical or virtual, into brand awareness, pipeline, and lasting relationships. This role is part of our marketing team and works cross-functionally with Sales and Partnerships to run Chili Piper's global event strategy. You'll have real ownership of the calendar and where we show up, not just the execution. You'll shape the annual plan, then make it happen: logistics, promotion, on-site, and follow-up, all the way through to measurable impact. This is a hands-on role. You're the one building the landing pages, pulling the CRM lists, and running the show on-site, not handing a brief to an agency and waiting. It's a strong fit for someone who is organized and proactive, thinks creatively about how we show up, and brings original ideas and a sense of humor to every event. It's fully remote, with travel to events as needed. What you'll do Own the annual event calendar. Decide, with marketing leadership, where Chili Piper should have a presence and why, and protect that focus as new opportunities come up Bring original ideas, creativity, and humor to how we show up, so our events feel like Chili Piper and not like everyone else's Manage execution end to end. Logistics, budgets, venues, vendors, shipments, swag, and on-site coordination, done by you and tracked by you Run event promotion from start to finish. Build event and webinar landing pages, export and segment contact lists from Salesforce and HubSpot to target the right attendees by city or segment, and send invites, reminders, and follow-ups independently Produce our virtual events and webinars end to end, from speaker prep and rehearsal to running the live show Collaborate across teams. With Marketing on branding, design, and promotion; with Sales to identify and invite the right prospects and customers; with Partnerships to coordinate sponsors and activations Ensure smooth on-site execution. Keep schedules on track and deliver a seamless experience from load-in to last handshake Build and nurture community. Deepen our relationships with GTM leaders, partners, and community members so our events compound over time Track performance. Collect attendee data, measure engagement, and report on outcomes and pipeline impact Amplify results. Work with Marketing to repurpose event content, including photos, videos, and testimonials, for social and post-event communication Manage vendors and budgets. Source partners, negotiate rates, and keep quality high and costs in check Run the debrief on every event and turn what you learn into a stronger program next time What we're looking for Builder mindset. You don't wait for someone to tell you how, you figure it out Tech-savvy operator. You know your way around CRM exports, spreadsheets, event tools, and email automation Hands-on doer. You do the execution and track the results yourself Creative problem-solver. When a venue cancels or a vendor flakes, you find a workaround fast, and when the format is stale, you invent a better one Organized and proactive. You turn chaos into systems and think two steps ahead Strong communicator. You coordinate cross-functional teams, vendors, and execs smoothly Customer-first. You care about memorable, frictionless experiences from invite to post-event follow-up Curious and eager to learn. You're always exploring new tools, trends, and ideas, including AI, to make each event better than the last Experience 2+ years in event management, field marketing, or community roles, ideally in B2B SaaS Proven ability to plan and execute events, from small dinners to large activations Hands-on experience with CRM tools like Salesforce and HubSpot, and event platforms like Luma, Zoom Webinars or similar Comfortable building simple landing pages, managing email lists, and running event promotion campaigns Skilled in vendor sourcing, budget tracking, and on-site coordination Strong cross-functional collaboration with Marketing, Sales, and Partnerships Excellent organizational and communication skills, with the ability to work independently and manage shifting priorities Familiar with tracking and reporting event performance, including attendance, engagement, and pipeline impact Experience managing partner collaborations or maintaining relationships with GTM leaders and communities is a plus Nice to have Experience in B2B SaaS, RevOps, or MarTech Prior involvement in partner activations or co-marketing events Experience managing sponsorships or collaborations with other brands Comfortable using analytics tools to measure event outcomes A strong network within the GTM, Sales, or Marketing communities Background in social or content amplification around events, for example capturing and repurposing event moments Interview process Application review. We'll review your background and experience to make sure there's a good fit for the role. Culture add interview. A first chat to get to know you: what drives you, how you like to work, and what unique perspective you'd bring to Chili Piper. Assessment. A short, practical assignment to see how you think and approach a real events challenge. It's not a test, we just want to see your creativity and thought process. Executive interview. The final step. We'll talk about your bigger picture, your passion for the space, your understanding of our product, and why Chili Piper feels like the right next step for you. TL;DR We're not hiring a "planner." We're hiring someone who can own the full experience, from the CRM export to the on-site execution to the community that keeps growing after everyone goes home, and turn GTM moments into momentum and measurable results. If that sounds like you, we want to talk. Additional Information Why you'll love being a part of our team: Our team loves Chili Piper because we’re building the company of the future. Work with an immensely talented global team Work in a business that’s run fairly and transparently Competitive pay based on market rate wherever you live We lead by example--showing industry peers and leaders how to innovate, improve, and grow--while having fun How we work: Freedom and flexibility. We’re a 100% distributed team working from around the world, and we've been fully remote since 2016. Our team members can work from wherever they want in the world, as long as they show up on our weekly all hands meeting on Zoom. Solve interesting problems. The software landscape has exploded. There are dozens of solutions for each problem. We want to be different. We come up with new angles on existing problems or invent better solutions to help companies with their sales and marketing. Then we turn these ideas into beautiful, smart software. Autonomy and ownership. Working on a distributed team means you don’t have someone micromanaging you or looking over your shoulder to make sure you’re getting things done. We’re a team of do-ers who take full ownership for their results. Be helpful. Our first value as a company is help. Help our customers be successful. Help our prospects get the right information and make the right decision whether or not it includes our products. Help our team members reach their full potential. The perks: Unlimited vacation (and we do mean it, and we do take it!) Generous health, dental, and vision insurance Any equipment/software/tech that you need to do your job Annual professional development stipend of $2,000 USD Equity - all Pipers receive stock options Annual company retreat in epic locations (past trips: Paris, Morocco, Tulum, Iceland, Ibiza, India). Check out the video from last year’s retreat in Tenerife.

input.description: About Golden Child Golden Child is redefining pet nutrition through an uncompromising focus on health, quality, and culinary craftsmanship. A Miami-based startup, we bring together veterinary nutrition expertise, classically trained chefs, and supply chain specialists to develop food held to human-grade standards. Our chef-crafted, science-backed Mains and functional Drizzles are designed to support lifelong health. We’re building a brand for people whose dogs are family, grounded in the care that goes into their food and the pleasure of the life they share. The Role Golden Child is looking for a Head of Brand & Creative to lead the next chapter of the brand and build the team that brings it to life. You will own Golden Child’s creative direction across packaging, campaigns, content, digital experiences, and physical activations. Your immediate focus will be carrying our evolving brand direction through the rebrand and relaunch, while establishing the creative capabilities we need as the business grows. Our ambition includes packaging people want in their homes, original films that reveal the people and decisions behind our recipes, and experiences that bring dog owners together. You’ll connect those expressions through a recognizable point of view, with food and the relationship between dogs and their people at the center. This is a highly hands-on role. You’ll move between setting brand strategy and shaping the work itself: developing concepts, directing shoots, reviewing packaging proofs, refining copy, and helping the team get projects out into the world. You will work closely with our CMO and founding team, alongside Growth, Culinary, Veterinary Nutrition, Product, and Operations. What You’ll Own 1. Brand Strategy & Creative Direction Own Golden Child’s positioning, visual identity, and tone of voice, translating the brand strategy into clear direction the team can use. Lead the rebrand across customer touchpoints, preserving what makes Golden Child recognizable while developing its next expression. Set the creative standard for design, photography, film, and copy. Make clear decisions and give feedback that improves the work. 2. Packaging & Physical Brand Experience Lead creative development across food packaging, shipping materials, and the experience of receiving and serving Golden Child. Partner with Product, Operations, and packaging specialists to take designs from concept through artwork, material selection, physical proofs, and production. Develop a packaging system that can accommodate new products and future retail channels, with clear product information and a consistent brand identity. Guide the design of merchandise and mealtime accessories as those opportunities develop. 3. Original Content & Storytelling Build an editorial and content plan around Golden Child’s food, veterinary nutrition expertise, and the lives people share with their dogs. Develop recurring formats, including films that follow our culinary and nutrition teams through recipe development, alongside portraits of owners and their dogs. Turn technical expertise into stories people want to watch and can understand. Work with our experts to keep nutritional explanations accurate. Plan long-form films and shorter edits together, giving each format a clear purpose across social, the website, email, and paid media. 4. Campaigns & Creative Performance Lead campaign concepts and creative execution for the relaunch, product introductions, and ongoing customer acquisition and retention. Partner with Growth to develop and test advertising, using performance findings to improve concepts, messaging, and execution. Translate larger brand stories into useful assets for each channel, including product pages, customer education, and lifecycle communications. Evaluate work against its intended purpose, from audience attention and engagement to conversion and repeat purchase. 5. Influencer, Tastemaker & Brand Partnerships Help shape the creative direction of Golden Child’s creator and tastemaker programs, helping identify people whose relationship with their dogs makes them a credible fit. Work with the CMO and Social Media Lead to develop collaborations that give participants meaningful access to the food and the people behind it, with room for their own perspective. Guide partner briefs, content concepts, gifting, and campaign integration in collaboration with the team managing those relationships. Identify opportunities across food, hospitality, fashion, beauty, and wellness that fit Golden Child’s audience and brand direction. 6. IRL Events & Community Experiences Lead the creative concept and brand expression of pop-ups, dinners, kitchen visits, and other gatherings for people and their dogs. Work with internal teams and external partners on the details that shape the experience, including the setting, food presentation, printed materials, and photography. Plan how each activation will reach people before and after the event through content and customer follow-up. Partner with Growth and Operations to define the objective, budget, and practical requirements before production begins. 7. Creative Team & Production Build and lead a lean internal creative team, supported by specialist freelancers, agencies, and production partners. Own creative briefs, production budgets, schedules, and delivery. Establish a reliable process for making ambitious work within an early-stage company. Direct photography and video production from concept through casting, crews, locations, post-production, and usage rights. Determine which capabilities Golden Child should build internally and where external specialists will make the work stronger. What We’re Looking For 8+ years of experience in brand and creative roles, including leadership of a multidisciplinary team or substantial creative programs. A portfolio showing a distinctive point of view and strong execution across several of the following: brand identity, packaging, campaigns, photography, film, and digital. input.description: About ElevenLabs ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. How we work High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. What we offer Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy. Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. About the role ElevenMusic is our AI music creation platform, letting anyone turn an idea into a finished, studio-grade track in minutes, with control over genre, mood, structure, and vocals across multiple languages. It is one of the most exciting parts of the ElevenCreative suite, and we want its voice, community, and content presence to match the ambition of the product. We are looking for a Content Creator & Strategist to own how ElevenMusic shows up in the world. You will make music with the platform every day, push it to its limits, and turn what you discover into educational content, tutorials, and social posts that teach creators what's possible. You will own the ElevenMusic social accounts, build and energise the community around the product, and represent ElevenMusic on stage at creator events. This is a hands-on role at the intersection of music creation, content, and community. The right person is a genuine music maker who lives on social platforms, has strong opinions about how an AI music brand should show up, and is just as comfortable behind a mic or on stage as they are in an editing timeline. Because you'll be using the product harder than almost anyone, you'll also be a critical feedback loop into the engineering team, shaping the product itself. What you will do Create educational content and tutorial videos around ElevenMusic, recording, editing, and formatting them natively for each platform, and publish them across our socials Make music with ElevenMusic constantly, testing the platform to its limits and turning experiments into content that shows creators what's possible Provide structured, high-signal product feedback to the engineering team based on deep daily use, helping shape the roadmap Own and manage the ElevenMusic social accounts, from content calendar and strategy through to publishing, engagement, and analytics Help build and grow a community around ElevenMusic, sparking conversation, surfacing creator feedback, and championing standout work Speak at creator events, representing ElevenMusic through talks, demos, and workshops Plan and execute content around product launches and feature releases, coordinating with product, engineering, and Marketing Stay ahead of trends in music creation, AI tools, and platform culture to find opportunities for the brand Requirements Demonstrated experience creating music and music-related content, with a portfolio of work you can share, you are a genuine music maker, not just a marketer Proven ability to produce educational content and tutorial videos end-to-end: recording, editing, adding text and motion, and formatting natively for platforms like X, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Experience managing social media accounts for a technology, music, or creative tools company, including content calendars, copywriting, and analytics Comfortable presenting publicly, speaking at events, running demos or workshops, and being a visible face for the product A genuine understanding of the AI and music creation landscape, you use the tools, follow the space, and have informed opinions about where things are headed Bonus Experience building or growing a creator community (Discord, forums, or similar) Background as a working musician, producer, or music educator with an existing audience Experience giving product feedback or working closely with engineering/product teams Experience with social scheduling and management tools (Sprout Social, Later, Buffer, or similar) Multilingual capabilities Growth Potential We believe in hiring the best talent in the world to make an impact in the right role at the right time. At ElevenLabs, strong performance creates opportunities for growth. Here are some of the career paths you can expect after excelling in this role: Lead content and community strategy across ElevenMusic as the product and team scale Move into a broader creative or content role spanning video, editorial, and social across ElevenLabs brands Expand into creator partnerships, evangelism, or brand marketing as the growth team evolves Location This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, Madrid, Warsaw and many more. #LI-Remote We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

input.description: About Kaseya Kaseya is the leading provider of AI-powered IT management and cybersecurity software, serving Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and internal IT organizations worldwide. Our comprehensive platform helps organizations efficiently manage, secure, and automate their IT environments, driving operational efficiency and long-term business success. Backed by Insight Partners , a leading global software investor, Kaseya has experienced sustained double-digit growth and continues to expand its global footprint. Today, Kaseya supports customers in more than 20 countries and manages over 15 million endpoints worldwide. Founded in 2000, Kaseya was built by builders - and we're still building. We look for people who create rather than wait, who see a hard problem and lean in, and who treat challenges as raw material. At Kaseya, everyone plays a role in shaping the future of IT: whether you're in engineering, product, sales, marketing, customer support, or operations, your work helps protect, defend, and optimize IT environments across the globe. We're building teams that grow, perform, and make an impact. If you're driven by the itch to make things better - a product, a process, a career - you'll fit right in. At Kaseya, we don't just raise the bar. We build it. The Director of Program Management, Global Events will lead the program management function within Kaseya's Global Events organization. This role owns how Kaseya's global event portfolio is planned, governed, resourced, and measured, turning strategy into an integrated, predictable, and scalable operating model across every region and event type. Reporting directly to the Vice President of Global Events, this leader will oversee the end-to-end program management of Kaseya's flagship conferences, regional events, executive experiences, customer and partner programs, sales kickoffs. The role leads a team of event program managers, sets the standards and tools they use, and connects Events with Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Product, Finance, and Leadership, ensuring every program is delivered on time, on budget, and with measurable business impact. Key Responsibilities Portfolio Strategy & Planning Partner with the VP of Global Events to translate the global event strategy into an integrated annual and multi-year portfolio plan. Own the global events calendar, balancing business priorities, regional needs, budget, and team capacity. Lead event intake, business case review, and prioritization, ensuring every investment is tied to clear objectives such as pipeline, customer retention, and brand. Run portfolio planning and business reviews with senior stakeholders, recommending where to invest, scale, consolidate, or retire programs. Program Governance & Operating Model Build and lead the Events Program Management team, defining the frameworks, phase gates, and decision rights used to deliver every event. Create standardized playbooks, templates, timelines, RACI models, and run-of-show standards that scale across event types and regions. Establish a consistent planning cadence, including status reporting, risk reviews, and executive checkpoints, that gives leadership clear visibility across the portfolio. Drive continuous improvement through post-event retrospectives, lessons learned, and process optimization. Cross-Functional Program Leadership Lead complex, multi-workstream programs such as flagship conferences and global sales kickoffs, coordinating content, registration, marketing, sales, production, logistics, and executive involvement. Align stakeholders across Marketing, Sales, Product Marketing, Product, Finance, Legal, and regional teams on scope, timelines, and success criteria. Manage dependencies, critical paths, and scope changes across concurrent programs, escalating and resolving issues quickly. Serve as a trusted advisor to executive stakeholders, providing clear recommendations and tradeoffs. Budget, Resource & Vendor Management Own consolidated financial management for the global events portfolio, including multimillion-dollar budgeting, multi-currency forecasting, and variance reporting. Lead resource and capacity planning across the program management team, agencies, and freelance partners. Drive global sourcing strategy and lead negotiations with venues, agencies, production partners, and suppliers, using portfolio scale to improve value. Establish vendor performance standards, service levels, and scorecards to ensure exceptional delivery. Systems, Data & Reporting Own the events technology and tooling roadmap, including project management, registration, event platforms, and their integration with CRM and marketing automation. Define and track portfolio KPIs includes budget adherence, attendee satisfaction, pipeline contribution, revenue influence, and event ROI. Deliver executive dashboards and portfolio reporting with actionable recommendations. Use data and insights to improve planning accuracy, operational efficiency, and business outcomes. Team Leadership & Development Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing global team of event program managers. Define roles, career paths, and competency standards for event program management. Foster a culture of accountability, ownership, collaboration, and operational discipline. Develop talent through coaching, mentorship, succession planning, and professional development. Required Qualifications 10+ years of experience in event program management, event operations, or a related program management role, including 5+ years leading teams. 10+ Proven success managing a global portfolio of large-scale conferences, customer and partner events, executive programs, sales kickoffs, and trade shows across multiple regions. 10+ Demonstrated experience building or leading a PMO, or establishing program governance, standardized processes, and scalable operating models. 5+ Experience owning multimillion-dollar budgets, multi-currency forecasting, contract negotiations, and vendor partnerships. Preferred Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Event Management, or a related field. Experience within technology, cybersecurity, IT services, or high-growth organizations. Advanced proficiency with project and portfolio management tools (e.g., Smartsheet, Asana, Monday.com, Jira), event management platforms (e.g., Cvent), and CRM and marketing automation systems (e.g., Salesforce, Marketo, HubSpot). Strong knowledge of international event logistics, risk management, and compliance requirements. Exceptional program management skills, including planning, prioritization, dependency management, and risk mitigation across concurrent programs. Strong executive presence and the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels, often without direct authority. Experience leading distributed teams in fast-paced, growth-oriented environments. Ability to travel domestically and internationally as required Additional information Kaseya provides equal employment opportunity to all employees and applicants without regard to race, religion, age, ancestry, gender, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, veteran status, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

The total compensation package for this role will include benefits. *This position may be performed remotely in most states within the US, with some exclusions **While this role offers the flexibility to work remotely, we have office hubs in Los Angeles and New York, where you can join in on learning and development opportunities, fun events, take advantage of a space to work, and collaborate in person! ***This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship Important Notice: Beware of Job Scams Wpromote recruiting communications will only be sent through our official channels via wpromote.com email addresses. input.title: Product Marketing

organization.name: Roboflow
organization.notes: Company website not supplied. Links open the source listing; confirm all requirements with the employer.

input.description: Who We Are Our mission is to make the world programmable. Sight is one of the key ways we understand the world, and soon this will be true for the software we use, too. We're building the tools, community, and resources needed to make the world programmable with artificial intelligence. Roboflow simplifies building and using computer vision models. Today, over 1M+ developers, including those from half the Fortune 100, use Roboflow's machine learning open source and hosted tools. That includes counting cells to accelerate cancer research, improving construction site safety, digitizing floor plans, preserving coral reef populations, guiding drone flight, and much more. Roboflow is supported by great customers and investors, having raised over $63 million from Y Combinator, Google Ventures, Craft Ventures, Sam Altman, Lachy Groom, amongst other leading software investors. Roboflowers are passionate builders who value ownership, accountability, and a bias toward action. We're curious, hands-on with new tech, and prefer showing our work over talking about it. Many of us have a founder mindset and thrive in our high-autonomy environment. What You'll Do Roboflow is in the middle of one of the biggest narrative shifts in our history. We are moving from being known as a data labeling tool for developers to being known as the Vision AI platform that powers production deployments inside the world's largest companies. Half the Fortune 100 already uses us. The next phase is making sure they, and the buyers inside them, see us that way. Own positioning end-to-end: Define how we talk about products and features. You will sharpen the messaging, build the proof, and make sure every external facing surface tells a coherent story. Lead product launches: Architect launches that land. Pick the moments that matter, build the narrative arc, line up the customer references, brief the analysts, and equip the field. You know what a great launch looks like and you've run them before. Build the buyer surfaces: Buyer facing landing pages, ROI frameworks, vertical specific narratives, customer outcomes, named reference stories. The website and content library should serve buyers as well as they serve developers. Deliver content that sales actually uses: Decks, battle cards, objection handling, competitive intel, pricing positioning. Talk to AEs every week. Build the materials they will actually use in a live deal. Productize customer proof: Turn customer wins into structured outcomes led case studies, video, webinars, conference talks, and peer referral motion. Operationalize the reference machine. Drive vertical strategy: Industrial, logistics, aerospace and defense, automotive, energy, healthcare. Help decide where to lean in, then build the vertical-specific messaging, content, and field motion to win there. Who You Are You've owned positioning end-to-end. Not just executed someone else's narrative. You've sat in front of the whiteboard, talked to 30 customers, written the messaging house, gotten leadership aligned, and rolled it out across the company. You can show us examples. You've led product launches that moved the needle. You can name specific launches, what your role was, what the inputs were, and what the result was. You sweat the inputs because you know the difference between a launch that lands and one that disappears. B2B experience. You've marketed to B2B buyers with $150K+ ACVs and complex sales cycles. You understand how Heads of AI and C-suite buyers make decisions, and you've built materials for each. Technical fluency. You should be comfortable in a technical conversation. Computer vision, ML infrastructure, or developer tools background is a strong plus. Excellent writer. Crisp, plain, specific. You can write the deck, the landing page, the email, and the script for a sales call. You cut filler. Sales partnership instinct. You like working with sales. You know how to embed with the field, attend deal reviews, learn what's actually winning, and bring it back into marketing. High output, low ego. You will move fast across a lot of surfaces. You will get feedback from a lot of people. You build the work, hold the bar, and ship. Who You'll Be Working With You will work directly with our Marketing Lead, our sales team, our co-founders, product leadership, and customer success. Your work shows up in every deal in the pipeline. Our team's backgrounds range from high school whiz kids, former founders of technology companies and fashion lines, world-class engineers, CMOs to CEOs, and have experience scaling businesses to millions in revenue. We want to work with exceptional people with a diverse background. At this stage, you'll have the ability to work cross-functionally with many members of the team and solve a wide array of problems. Where You'll Work We currently have Hubs in New York City and San Francisco with a mindset of opening more offices as we grow. We provide opportunities (like team onsites in different cities ) and resources (like a travel stipend) to work in person with other team members as much as you'd like, while also supporting remote team members. You can work from one of our Hubs, work from home, work at co-working spaces, etc. We want you to work where you work best. Learn more about how we work at Roboflow . What You'll Receive To determine your salary, we use a number of market and data-driven salary sources. We review all salaries every 6 months to ensure we stay in line with the market. In addition to our cash compensation, we offer generous perks and benefits. Below are some of the highlights: $3500/yr Travel Stipend to travel anywhere anytime to work alongside other Roboflowers. $350/mo productivity stipend to spend on things that make your work environment more productive, like high speed internet at home or a co-working space. Cover up to 100% of your health insurance costs for you and your partner or family. Equity in the company so we are all invested in the future of computer vision. Interview Process Below is the interview process you can expect for this role. You will be speaking directly with our team about what it's like to work and thrive here. Introduction Phase: [45m] Meet with hiring manager, Trevor Lynn, to assess for overall mindset and skill set This first interview is a time to get to know more about the role, allow us to get to know you better, and ensure it's a good fit for both parties to continue moving forward in the process Team Interview Phase: [60m] Meet with a member of our marketing team [60m] Meet with a member of our product or marketing team [30m] Meet with hiring manager, Trevor Lynn Use this time to review specifics about the job description and ask questions before the project phase begins. Project Phase: You'll build a project within a specified amount of time. Expect something that resembles real PMM work: a positioning exercise, a launch plan for a real or hypothetical Roboflow release, or a sales-enablement asset for a specific buyer. We check references and conduct a background check. Final Interview Stage: [60m] Meet with Co-founder & CTO, Brad Dwyer or Joseph Nelson, Co-founder & CEO Note: you are welcome to request additional conversations with anyone you would like to meet and we will accommodate as best we can.

input.title: Global Field & Event Marketing Lead

organization.name: Nash
organization.notes: Company website not supplied. Links open the source listing; confirm all requirements with the employer.

input.description: Nash is the autonomic logistics platform. Self-optimizing, self-healing AI Agents unify decisioning and execution across fleets, carriers, and fulfillment networks. Set the objective, and the system runs until you hit it. We’re 1,000+ customers across 20+ countries, backed by a16z and Y Combinator. About this role Nash is hiring its first global field and event marketing lead. You will own how Nash shows up in person: the event strategy for the company, and the field execution behind it in every region. You will build the event calendar with our regional GTM leads, and lead a team of regional field managers across APAC, EMEA and North America. You report to the VP of Growth and work directly with Sales leaders in each region. What you own The event calendar. You decide which shows and sponsorships earn a place, and how big Nash goes at each one. The account list for each event, shared with Sales, so events and outreach point the same way. What each event returned, and what that says about where Nash shows up next. The field budget across regions, invested against pipeline and deal acceleration. Every in-person moment Nash creates: booths, dinners, hosted events, gifting, merch and swag. ABM events for our top accounts, built with the account teams. Executive dinners, onsites, and gifts made for one account at a time. The relationships with show organizers, partners and vendors that earn speaking slots, better booth placement, and co-hosted events. Vendors and production partners in every region. You choose them, set the terms, and hold them to the standard, across booth build, print, swag, freight and storage. The content each event produces. You shoot your own, direct photographers and videographers, and get attendees and the team posting. Internal events, including all-hands and company offsites, held to the same standard as the ones customers see. The regional team. You hire the field managers, set the standard, and keep running the events that matter most yourself. What you bring 7+ years in B2B field or event marketing, across more than one region. Shows you owned outright. You picked them, ran them, and answered for what came back. You have run an event people wanted to come to and talked about afterward. One you were proud of, and that became a flagship part of the company. A team you built and led across time zones, employees or contractors, including the hiring. Super self-starter. You find the person who can unblock you, and you can put something good together on budget and with days' notice, then build the system that makes the next one easier to run. Taste and polish. You know the difference between a booth people stop at and one they walk past, and the details guests notice are right, from the invite through the run of show. Pipeline and the big picture. You can walk through the pipeline your events produced and how it moved, and you plan a year of events as one program rather than a series of one-offs. AI already in your workflow, and something you built or improved that you can show us. Command of budget and logistics at scale, and steadiness in the week of a show. Willingness to travel 30 to 40% of the year. How to Apply Send us your resume, links or photos of events you have run, and a short note on the one you are proudest of and why. If you would rather skip the cover letter and send a Loom walking us through that event, the invite that filled the room, or the run of show behind it, that is very much encouraged. Want to grab our attention and bypass the Recruiting platform? Record a video introducing yourself at testimonials.nash.ai with code JOIN-NASH. Your application pings us in Slack the moment it lands. If you are show ready at 8am on the first morning of a conference, this is nothing. More about Nash Nash is the platform that powers modern logistics. Commerce has inverted. For decades, customers came to where products and services were. Now products and services come to them, on their terms, in real time. That shift has turned every company into a logistics company, even though almost none of them were built to be one. Couriers, fleets, gig workers, parcel carriers, in-store labor, and increasingly autonomous systems all have to be coordinated in real time, against tighter windows and rising expectations, with hard-fought customer trust on the line. Nash unifies decisioning, execution, and capacity into a single programmable platform. Real-time, AI-native intelligence determines what should happen, operational control executes it, and the platform dynamically orchestrates capacity from any source: a company's own fleets, partners, or the Nash delivery network. Whether a job involves a courier, a gig driver, an internal fleet, a store employee, a technician, or an autonomous vehicle, Nash selects the right resource and manages execution through completion. We power delivery and logistics for some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, 7-Eleven, and Woolworths, alongside platforms like Shopify and Toast. Over the next decade, logistics will become as foundational to commerce as payments, cloud, and connectivity. Nash is the platform that powers it. Nash was founded in 2021 by Mahmoud Ghulman (2x Founder, MIT) and Aziz Alghunaim (2x Founder, 2x YC, Ex-Palantir, MIT) and is backed by Y Combinator, a16z, and other top investors. We are headquartered in San Francisco. What You’ll Love About Us ✅ Early-stage, well-funded startup – directly impact the company and grow your career! ✅ Quarterly broader team on-sites to bond with teammates ✅ Competitive compensation and opportunity for equity ✅ Flexible paid time off ✅ Health, dental, and vision insurance for US employees

input.description: About Cantina Cantina Labs is a social AI company, developing a suite of advanced real-time models that push the boundaries of expression, personality, and realism. We bring characters to life, transforming how people tell stories, connect, and create. We build and power ecosystems. Cantina, our flagship social AI platform, is just the beginning. If you're excited about the potential AI has to shape human creativity and social interactions, join us in building the future! About the Role We’re working on real-time video generation for interactive characters, spanning realistic humans, stylized characters, and non-human identities. We want these characters to feel present: to speak, react, and express themselves through their face, gestures, and body language. This brings together a set of closely connected research problems. A character needs a consistent appearance, expressive and coherent motion, and a natural relationship between speech and movement. The model also needs to respond quickly and keep generating reliably as an interaction unfolds. Quality, controllability, and efficiency all matter. You’ll work across streaming generation, fine-tuning, distillation, inference optimization, and data. Some problems will call for a new training approach; others will come down to better examples, a more useful evaluation, or understanding a bottleneck in the implementation. Part of the job is figuring out which intervention is worth making. You’ll have substantial freedom to propose directions, investigate unfamiliar ideas, and shape what we work on next. We’re looking for someone who enjoys that freedom and can turn it into a steady sequence of useful experiments. What You’ll Work On Real-time and streaming generation. Develop models that support responsive interaction while maintaining visual quality and consistency over time. Investigate latency, continuity, and how model behavior changes during longer generation. Character expression and motion. Explore how appearance, facial expression, gesture, and body movement come together into a coherent character. Improve the relationship between speech and motion across different identities and visual styles. Fine-tuning and post-training. Adapt video models to new data, behaviors, and capabilities. Investigate training objectives and conditioning methods, and follow promising ideas through implementation and evaluation. Distillation and inference optimization. Make generation faster and more efficient. Work across model-level approaches and runtime improvements, measuring their effects on quality, latency, and memory. Data development. Spend meaningful time with the actual training examples. Identify missing coverage and recurring failure modes, improve curation and sampling, and develop data that helps models learn the behavior we want. Evaluation. Build comparisons that make progress visible and failures understandable. Combine quantitative measurements with careful inspection of generated video and the experience of interacting with the model. Research and collaboration. Read relevant work, reproduce and adapt useful ideas, and share early experiments, demos, and findings. Help the team decide what deserves more time and compute. What You’ll Bring Experience training or fine-tuning video or related generative models. Ability to learn unfamiliar methods quickly and turn ideas into useful experiments. Good experimental judgment, ownership, and clear communication. You’ll have freedom to explore new approaches. We expect fast iteration and early sharing of results. Compensation When determining compensation, a number of factors will be considered, including skills, experience, job scope, location, and competitive compensation market data. Benefits for U.S.-based roles: Competitive salary and generous company equity Medical, dental, and vision insurance – 99.99% of premiums covered by Cantina 42 days of paid time off, including: 15 PTO days 10 sick days 15 company holidays 2 floating holidays Generous parental leave & fertility support 401(k) retirement savings plan Lifestyle spending account – $500/month to use however you’d like Complimentary lunch and snacks for in-office employees One Medical membership, and more!

input.title: Event Manager, India

organization.name: Contour Education
organization.notes: Company website not supplied. Links open the source listing; confirm all requirements with the employer.

input.description: This is a remote position. Event Manager, India Remote (India) | Full-Time Also searched as: Event Coordinator, Event Project Manager, Event Operations Manager, Project Manager Could you deliver a flawless day for hundreds of students in a city you have never set foot in? On a typical day you might walk a venue coordinator in Melbourne through your room and AV requirements in the morning, lock catering numbers against the live registration count and follow up two presenter confirmations with the academic team after lunch, and update the run sheet and brief the on-ground leads before you log off. About Contour We started in 2020 with a handful of students and a belief that great education should not be out of reach. Today we operate across three brands with 8,000+ students and 425+ team members: roughly 100 in India and 325 onshore in Australia. The India team runs publishing, student experience, CRM and technology, operations, and people and culture, and this role sits with the events function that delivers Contour's event calendar across Australia. A great event looks effortless to the family walking in. Someone has to be the reason it looks that way. About This Role You are the dedicated project manager behind Contour's events. The calendar runs from full exam simulation days for hundreds of students to revision lecture series selling thousands of tickets across Victoria and Queensland, with parent workshops and online sessions in between. You take each one from first brief to post-event review: timeline, venue, suppliers, registration milestones, comms deadlines, run sheet, event-day coordination, wrap-up. You report to the Chief Marketing Officer (CMO). The CMO owns marketing strategy and the onshore event-day call when someone must be in the room. Everything else about how events get planned and delivered is yours. Marketing owns promotion, creative, and the registration campaigns. Academics owns session content and who presents it. Operations owns student data and check-in technology. On event day, teams on the ground in Australia execute in the room. The plan that ties them together, the dates they all work to, and the accountability for the day landing well: those are yours. Two qualities separate a strong hire from an average one here. First, you think in dependencies: you see that catering numbers hang off registration close, which hangs off a reminder email, which hangs off a presenter confirming a title, and you fix the weak link three weeks early instead of discovering it three days out. Second, you follow up without souring relationships: you ask specifically, escalate when twice was enough, and people still enjoy working with you. One more reality worth naming: you will rarely be in the room. You run events from India that are delivered in Australia, which means your plans, run sheets, and briefings have to be strong enough that the day runs without you standing in it. You start as the sole dedicated event project manager, plugged into established marketing, academic, operations, and student experience teams. The calendar has grown faster than the way it is run: the biggest series now sell out lecture theatres, and until now no single person has owned how events get delivered. You build that playbook: the standard project plan, the run sheet format, the review loop that makes each event sharper than the last. By the end of month three, you will have taken at least one major event from brief through delivery to review, built the project plan and run sheet templates the team reuses, and mapped the full calendar with owners, dates, and dependencies visible to everyone involved. What you build in those months will run every event Contour delivers after them. Where the Work Lives monday.com: project plans and task ownership live here. Keeping status current is how a remote team knows an event is on track without asking. Google Sheets: run sheets, attendee lists, and event-day logistics. The people delivering the day work from your latest version, so document discipline is part of the job. Eventbrite: registrations and ticketing. You watch the numbers daily because rooms, catering, and comms decisions all key off them. HubSpot: student and guardian event comms run through it, alongside the lifecycle comms team. Slack: where cross-team, cross-timezone coordination happens, in writing. What You Will Do Own each event end to end. Scope, timeline, suppliers, delivery, invoices, review: nothing about the event is someone else's problem. Build and drive the project plan. Every task with an owner, a date, and a dependency in monday.com. When something slips, you catch it while there is still room to re-sequence. Keep the full event calendar visible. Every event, owner, and key date in one place in monday.com, so anyone can see what's coming without asking you. Coordinate Marketing, Academics, and Operations. Registration launches, presenter confirmations, resource handovers, comms milestones: you set the dates and hold every team to them. Lock venues and suppliers. Room requirements, AV, catering, printing, signage: briefed clearly, confirmed in writing, and settled before their cutoffs. Run registrations as a control signal. Work with the digital team on ticket setup in Eventbrite, track numbers daily, and trigger capacity, waitlist, and extra-session calls in good time, because 850 registrations against 760 seats is a problem you want weeks of notice on, not days. Write the run sheet and brief the day. Minute by minute, with named owners for every stage, and briefings that leave the teams in the room certain of their part. Close the loop. Attendance data, feedback, supplier invoices, a short post-event report, and fixes carried into the next plan. If a better tool exists for something we are doing manually, make the case and we will back it. Requirements What You Need 4 to 6 years delivering projects or events where you held the whole timeline, not a slice of it You have delivered work that depended on people who did not report to you, and it landed anyway Comfortable chasing and escalating. A quiet slip three weeks out becomes an event-day crisis, so persistence here is method, not personality, and the people you chase still want to work with you again. Writing that lands exactly as intended. Your documents are how a remote coordinator directs a live day, so they carry more weight than they would in an office Clean document and data habits: plans, lists, and versions other people can trust without checking with you Comfortable working across the India and Australia time difference, with the flexibility to be on deck when events go live Nice to Have You have run an event remotely, delivered in a city or country you were not in Events for education, exams, or student and family audiences Hands-on with monday.com, Eventbrite, or HubSpot Negotiating with venues and suppliers The Kind of People Who Thrive Here The people who do well here see a gap and close it without being asked, holding the bar even when the clock is short. They give a direct read on the work in front of them, including when it's wrong, and when their own idea doesn't hold up, they say so and bring a better one. They build something that keeps running after they step back. Problems here don't show up on schedule or in the same shape twice, and they'd rather make the right call on limited information than let something break while they wait for a sign-off. That's the job. They name the blocker and the ask the moment they have it, on a call or a text, because decisions get made on the information you bring. Contour's current cluster heads started as team leads. The path from operator to leader is real here. What Good Looks Like Nothing slips silently: every at-risk date is flagged with a re-plan attached, not just an apology. The day runs off the document: venue and floor teams execute from your run sheet without needing you on the phone every ten minutes. Stakeholders answer you: your asks are specific, dated, and easy to action, so people respond instead of stalling. Every event beats the last: reviews turn into changes in the next plan, not a document nobody opens. Benefits Fully remote, anywhere in India. The events themselves happen in Australia; you coordinate them from wherever you are, and onshore teams deliver on the day. Compensation details shared early in the hiring process. After you apply: a short screen, a practical planning task, then a culture conversation with our People team, and a final interview with the Chief Marketing Officer, in about four weeks. Apply with a CV and one paragraph on the most complex event or project you have delivered, and the moment it nearly went wrong. Originally posted on Himalayas

input.description: About the company At Nuitée , we are building the API backbone for the global travel industry. Founded in 2017, Nuitée is on a mission to transform a fragmented travel ecosystem with simple, scalable, and API-first infrastructure—think “Stripe for Travel.” By enabling seamless connectivity between hotels, OTAs, fintechs, super-apps, and businesses, some of which are entering the travel market for the first time, Nuitée empowers companies to deliver reliable travel products effortlessly. Our robust platform simplifies complex supplier networks, offering direct access to hotel inventory with better pricing, coverage, and technology. With teams across the globe, including hubs in London, New York, San Francisco, Palma de Mallorca and Casablanca, Nuitée has grown into a global infrastructure provider trusted by industry leaders like Hopper, Priceline, Google, and Uber. Now backed by leading VCs and world-class investors including leaders from , Stripe, and Shopify, Nuitée is positioned to redefine the B2B travel market, streamline operations for hotels, and enable new applications through cutting-edge APIs. Nuitée is at the forefront of a revolution—delivering AI-powered, smarter, and more personalized travel experiences for a new era. About the role Remote in EMEA, or hybrid in Barcelona. You'll decide how a category-defining travel company tells its story. Nuitée powers hotel booking for some of the biggest names in travel and fintech. The product and our partnerships have driven that growth, and the next step is telling the story at the scale the business has reached. You'll own Nuitée 's external voice end to end: brand, PR, events, and social. It starts with one story that works for both sides of our marketplace: the travel and fintech companies that distribute hotels, and the hotels themselves. Then you get that story in front of the right people, consistently. Marketing at Nuitée is a growth engine. Every story, announcement, and event should help open doors and drive revenue. You'll set the direction and get hands-on with the work, seeing your ideas through from first draft to launch. What you'll own: Brand & Creative Direction Own Nuitée 's positioning, narrative, and visual identity, and make sure the brand feels consistent and distinctive at every touchpoint. Build one story that resonates with travel platforms, fintechs, and hotels alike, and strengthen Nuitée 's reputation with hotels and supply partners. Set the creative direction for launches, campaigns, events, and presentations, and shape design work directly. PR & Communications Own PR end to end, from partner announcements and press releases to executive talking points and thought leadership. Build relationships with travel, tech, and business media, and plan the outlets and partnerships that matter each quarter. Raise the profile of Nuitée 's leadership through interviews, speaking slots, and industry commentary. Events & Experiences Build the events calendar with Sales: where Nuitée shows up across travel, tech, fintech, and AI, and how. Lead the concept, branding, and execution of events, from sponsorships to our own dinners and activations. Turn events into relationships and pipeline, and measure what each one delivers. Content & Social Build an editorial point of view for Nuitée across LinkedIn, the website, and other owned channels. Turn product launches, partnerships, and company milestones into stories, and help leaders and teams share them. Make complex infrastructure, APIs, and AI innovation simple and memorable. Digital Brand Own the brand experience across the website and key digital surfaces, working with Product and Growth. Build pages, assets, and content yourself, using AI tools to move fast. Building the Function Set up brand guidelines, templates, and processes so everyone at Nuitée tells the same story. Work with freelancers and partners where needed, and grow the function as it proves its impact Nuitée has grown 10x since 2022, was profitable before raising a $48M Series A led by Accel, and works with companies such as Revolut, Grab, Hopper, and Priceline. Telling that story well, to the right audiences, is now a priority for the business. This role fits if you: Have 6–8+ years across marketing, PR, communications, or events, building the brand of a fast-growing tech, SaaS, fintech, or travel-tech company. Can turn complex technical products into simple, compelling stories, and take them all the way to high-quality execution. Have led PR and media relations, including sensitive partner announcements, and are comfortable representing a company externally alongside senior leaders. Have created and delivered industry events, launches, or brand activations. Have a strong eye for design. You can direct creative work and build assets, pages, and content yourself, using AI tools to move faster. Are equally comfortable setting strategy and executing hands-on in a fast-moving environment. Bonus if you have travel industry experience, especially with hotels, hotel tech, or distribution, or an existing network across travel media and industry events. Nuitée moves quickly, keeps things simple, and gives people a lot of ownership. You’ll do well here if you’re comfortable making decisions, prefer shipping and learning over long planning cycles, and enjoy seeing your ideas go live within days. If this sounds like your kind of role, we'd love to hear from you. You can apply with your LinkedIn profile or CV. The process is straightforward and typically takes 2–3 weeks. Why Nuitee? At Nuitée , we’re not just reimagining travel—we’re building the infrastructure to power it. Massive Market Opportunity: We are tackling the $9.9tn travel industry, starting with the $75 billion B2B hotel market, a fragmented space filled with outdated systems, gatekeepers, and inefficiencies. Nuitée ’s API-first platform is solving this, enabling businesses to access hotel inventory seamlessly and at scale. World-Class Backing: Backed by Accel and visionary leaders across tech and travel—including Booking.com, Stripe, and Shopify—we’re equipped to scale our ambition globally. Bootstrapped Resilience, Startup Agility: Having grown profitably for years without external funding, we combine operational discipline with the speed and innovation of a scaling startup. Global Impact: Our infrastructure supports partners like Google, Grab, worldwide fintechs, superapps, travel companies and others AI-Driven Innovation: Nuitée is uniquely positioned to power the future of travel in the AI era—enabling seamless, intelligent, and hyper-personalized travel interactions. By joining Nuitée , you’ll be part of a team that’s building a category-defining platform. You’ll work on a global scale, innovate alongside industry leaders, and help drive the next phase of travel technology. If you’re excited to push boundaries, redefine a multi-trillion-dollar industry, and grow with us— Nuitée is the place for you. Your information will be stored securely and will only be retained for as long as necessary for the recruitment process, or up to 6 months afterward, in accordance with our data protection policy and applicable laws. input.description: Please note, this listing is not for an immediate open position but for our Talent Pool for Video Editors. Grip is building the infrastructure for enterprise content production—turning static master creatives into scalable, high-quality outputs through automation, AI workflows, and modular design systems. This role sits at the intersection of creative intent and production reliability. As a Video Editor , you’ll create final edits and market adaptations, making sure every version keeps the quality, creative direction, and brand standards of the approved master. You’ll work with large volumes of content and prepare assets for automated delivery. What You Will Do Replace VFX shots in final edits, checking timing, alignment, and consistency. Create cutdowns and adaptations that preserve the story and visual style. Resize and reframe videos for formats such as 9:16, 1:1, and 4:5. Check every delivery for video, audio, colour, and VFX issues, including single-frame errors. Fix or flag colour mismatches, compression issues, audio imbalance, and render errors. Export assets to the correct broadcast, social, and web specifications. Receive, check, and organise master files from vendors. Transcode files using the correct codecs, formats, and colour spaces, and create MP4 review files. Follow and improve editing and quality control workflows, finding solutions that can be applied across many versions. Prepare assets for automated pipelines and distribution. Work with project managers and VFX supervisors, apply creative feedback, and flag issues early. Act as the final quality check before assets enter production systems, ensuring deliveries are ready to use and on schedule. Requirements Who You Are You’re a detail-focused editor who cares about visual quality and understands how to keep it consistent across many versions. What You Bring Proven video editing experience with a strong portfolio across formats and platforms. Hands-on experience with Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects. An understanding of VFX workflows and post-production pipelines. Good knowledge of codecs, formats, transcoding, compression, and delivery specifications. Experience checking video, audio, and colour quality. Strong attention to detail and the ability to spot subtle inconsistencies. An organised approach to managing files, versions, and large volumes of content. The ability to learn new tools, solve problems, and work closely with creative and technical teams. Reliability under production deadlines. A fast, reliable internet connection, a powerful computer that can handle 4K footage, and enough storage for large project files. Why Join Grip? The Platform Position. Grip is infrastructure for enterprise creative production—powering content generation across global brands with strict quality requirements. The Market Timing. AI is increasing content volume exponentially. The bottleneck is no longer creation—it’s maintaining quality at scale. The Technical Moat. A multi-tenant platform combining AI workflow orchestration, ComfyUI integrations, and production-grade pipelines across TypeScript, Python, Elixir, and C#. The Work. You define what “quality” means in a system generating thousands of assets—and ensure it holds under scale. The procedure If you’re ready to bring your powers to a role where you can make a difference, we want to hear from you. Send your resume and portfolio in English via the link provided. If you have questions, contact our Recruitment Department at . After reviewing your application, if there’s a potential fit, a member of our recruitment team will be in touch with you. INDG Grip handles and uses personal data of job applicants in line with its Recruitment Privacy Policy . Originally posted on Himalayas

If you’re ready to do the most meaningful work of your career alongside people who are just as passionate as you are, you’re in the right place.
