If you are passionate about solving real-world problems and ideating beside the best and the brightest, we invite you to join us! This role is remote, but distance is no barrier to impact. Our hybrid teams collaborate across geographies to solve big problems, stay close to our customers, and grow together. You will be part of a culture that values trust, accountability, and shared success where your work truly matters. Job Summary The Technical Marketing Creative team brings complex cybersecurity stories to life through compelling, accessible, and visually ambitious creative work. As a Technical Marketing Creative Producer, you will partner closely with product experts to translate highly technical ideas into engaging visual experiences spanning video, motion design, and branded content. Operating like an internal creative studio, you will leverage strong storytelling, design thinking, production craft, and emerging AI tools to move quickly from idea to execution. We are seeking a conceptual thinker and hands-on creative who is curious about new technologies and excited to elevate the quality of technical marketing. Key Responsibilities Collaborate with creative leads and experts to turn complex cybersecurity topics into compelling creative concepts. Participate in brainstorming sessions and workshops, developing multiple approaches to creative briefs. Develop creative treatments, moodboards, storyboards, scripts, and pitch decks to communicate visual direction. Edit polished short-form and long-form video content using strong storytelling, pacing, and visual craft. Provide a strong specialty such as motion design, graphic design, 3D, VFX, or cinematography. Use generative AI and emerging tools to explore concepts, prototype ideas, and accelerate workflows. Strong eye for composition, typography, pacing, design, and visual storytelling. Ability to move comfortably between conceptual work and hands-on execution. Strong communication and collaboration skills. Curiosity and willingness to learn technical subject matter and translate it for broader audiences. Ability to manage multiple projects and adapt quickly as priorities evolve. Ability to travel for work and shoots. Preferred Qualifications Demonstrated strength in an additional creative discipline such as motion design, 3D, VFX, or art direction. organization.name: Darkroom
organization.notes: Company website not supplied. Links open the source listing; confirm all requirements with the employer.

input.description: About Darkroom Darkroom is the leading next-generation growth marketing firm engineering the brands of tomorrow. Founded in 2017, we set out to redefine what a modern agency could be, by replacing the inertia of legacy advertising behemoths with a model built for speed, intelligence, and measurable impact. At our core, Darkroom is a human services company powered by Shadow , a universal AI commerce layer that integrates executive-level strategy with proprietary agentic technology. This fusion enables our teams to deliver outsized returns by enhancing creative output, operational efficiency, and revenue generation across every stage of the customer journey. Our track record speaks for itself: billions in attributable revenue driven across e-commerce marketplaces, media networks, DTC ecosystems, and social commerce platforms. Every engagement feeds into our proprietary data infrastructure, enabling a continuous feedback loop that accelerates growth, improves margins, and compounds results across our client portfolio. What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos) . Our founders were recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 for advancing the intersection of technology, marketing, and advertising, cementing Darkroom 's role as a defining player in the future of media innovation. About the Role This is a dedicated, senior role on a single account, helping a key client bring a brand new product to market, with Darkroom owning all media channels. You are the creative lead on that engagement, accountable for the brand's whole creative story, from positioning and messaging down to the hook on a 15-second ad. That makes this different from a typical agency creative role. You are not spreading yourself across a portfolio. You are going deep on one enterprise client, setting creative positioning with their leadership, then sitting with designers and editors to tighten the frame across paid, social, and retention. What you'll do Responsibilities: Brand & Creative Positioning: Own creative positioning for the brand and its new product launch. Turn brand strategy, audience insight, and competitive context into a clear point of view on what a brand says and how it looks and sounds. Copy & Messaging: Lead copy and messaging end to end, from messaging frameworks, taglines, and campaign lines to ad copy, email, and SMS. Flex tone by channel and funnel stage, and be the person who delivers when a client asks you to "punch up the copy." Full-Funnel Creative Strategy: Lead creative strategy across paid (Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Amazon), organic social (Instagram, TikTok), and retention (email, SMS, lifecycle), so every channel ladders up to one brand story. Campaigns: Concept and lead the launch campaign and the large, integrated campaigns that follow, from the big idea through briefs, production, launch, and measuring what they actually did. Testing & Learning: Own the testing roadmap: what gets tested, in what order, against what hypothesis, and what a real win looks like before spend goes live. Balance brand-building work with performance. Hands-On Creative Direction: Work directly with Designers and Editors, briefing statics, motion, short-form video, UGC, and storyboards. Give sharp, tactical feedback on design, pacing, and edit structure, and jump into Figma or an edit yourself when it's faster. This isn't the role for strategy-only folks. Data Analysis: Read performance data across paid, social, and retention, from ad metrics to open rate, click rate, and repeat purchase, and turn it into the next concept. Executive Presentation & Client Leadership: Present creative strategy and campaigns to the client's leadership with clarity, confidence, and strategic rationale. Own the creative relationship on the account and navigate pushback with ease. Cross-Team Partnership: Work daily with Paid Media, Analytics, and the client's own program leads so creative and media run as one program. Team Leadership: Lead the creative team on the account, raise the bar on craft, and build the processes, frameworks, and AI-enabled workflows that keep quality high as volume grows. You should apply if this sounds like you 6+ years in creative strategy, brand marketing, or creative leadership, including 3+ years at Director level or above. Brand marketing experience. You've shaped positioning, messaging, and brand voice for consumer brands, in-house or agency side. Creative experience across paid, social, and retention. You've led work on Meta and TikTok ads, organic social, and email/SMS, and you understand how each channel works and where they connect. You've directed large-scale, integrated campaigns, including OOH, from the big idea through launch and results. You're a strong writer and lead copy and messaging yourself. A portfolio of proven brand-scale and go-to-market case studies, showing brand, performance, and campaign work across statics, short-form video, motion, OOH, and lifecycle, with context on the results it drove. You've owned production end to end, from brief and pre-production through shoot, post, and delivery, on time and on budget. You speak in hooks, angles, and metrics. You know thumb-stop rate, 3-second hold, hook retention, CTR, and CPA, and you use them to decide what to test next. You're comfortable working directly with designers and editors. You can storyboard, give frame-by-frame feedback, and jump into Figma or Adobe Creative Suite to polish assets. You already use tools like Claude, Midjourney, Perplexity, Runway, or similar to increase speed and volume. You have shipped work with AI-assisted elements, not just experiments. Soft skills Team management: You've managed and grown creative teams. You lead with clarity, direct feedback, and a high bar, and people want to work for you. Stakeholder management: You have enterprise client experience and keep everyone, from the client's C-suite to their program leads, aligned without slowing the work down. Communication: You're an excellent communicator, both in writing and when presenting to senior clients. Ownership: You take a program from brief to delivery and are accountable for the outcome, not just the idea. High EQ, low ego: You give and take direct feedback, stay calm under pressure, and know where every person on your team truly sits. Hard disqualifiers No brand marketing or positioning experience. Performance-only with no brand point of view is not a fit. No paid social creative experience on Meta or TikTok. Can't lead copy and messaging. No portfolio link or no results context. Strategy-only, with no hands-on work alongside designers and editors. Not excellent in client presentation and salesmanship. What It's Like to Work at Darkroom Darkroom is not a typical agency. We are looking for A players who want to build something great. We move fast, think deeply, and expect every team member to bring insight and rigor to everything they touch. We hold a high bar for performance, creativity, and ownership — but we also support each other relentlessly. No egos, no red tape — just world-class talent building something remarkable. We believe in autonomy with accountability, truth over comfort, and outcomes over optics. Unlimited PTO + US holidays: Rebooting is part of the work. Take the time you need to stay sharp. Remote-First Culture: Many roles are fully remote. Employees based in or near our New York or Lisbon HQs are expected to work hybrid with weekly in-office time. Hub locations include Brazil and Spain. Health & Wellness: Company-sponsored medical, dental, and vision coverage. Finances, growth, and retirement: Darkroom offers a robust 401(k) program with company match and profit-sharing opportunities to help you save and grow as the company grows. Parental Leave: Flexible parental leave to support new parents during this important transition. Growth: Our interdisciplinary model gives every Darkroom er exposure far beyond their core role. Grow your skills, expand your influence, and stay at the forefront of the industry. Compensation: The base salary range for this role is $160,000 to $220,000 per year. This range represents the anticipated minimum and maximum for this position and applies to candidates based in New York, including New York City, in compliance with the New York State Pay Transparency Law and the New York City Salary Transparency Law. Actual compensation within this range will be determined based on experience, skills, and qualifications. Equal Opportunity Statement Darkroom is an equal opportunity workplace, we are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national orientation, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. Originally posted on Himalayas

input.description: Foundation is an AI visibility marketing agency that drives pipeline growth for mid-market and enterprise B2B tech and SaaS companies. We help our clients generate pipeline through content engineered to distribute across LLMs, search, social, communities like Reddit, and every channel their buyers actually use. Mission of the Role The mission of the Marketing Strategist (YouTube) is to design and lead YouTube strategies that drive measurable business growth for our clients. YouTube is one of the highest-value GEO channels we invest in. It shapes what buyers watch, what Google surfaces, and what LLMs cite. This role owns channel strategy end to end: what gets made, who appears on camera, how each video is packaged, and how the program performs. It combines deep analytical thinking with strong creative instincts, partnering across teams, production partners, and clients to turn performance data into actionable strategy. Key Responsibilities Develop and execute comprehensive, data-driven YouTube strategies aligned with client objectives and pipeline goals. Analyze YouTube Analytics, VidIQ data, retention curves, search and suggested traffic, and LLM citation trends to uncover strategic opportunities for channel growth. Own packaging strategy across accounts: titles, thumbnails, hooks, descriptions, chapters, and Shorts. Source, vet, and brief on-camera talent and creators who fit each client's audience and category. Lead collaborative planning sessions with GEO/SEO, Creative, and production teams (internal and external partners) to ensure video programs operate as cohesive systems. Conduct recurring channel audits, identifying growth gaps and recommending improvements. Build scalable frameworks, playbooks, and documentation to standardize strategy execution across accounts. Use AI tools throughout the workflow (research, scripting support, optimization) to compress production time and cost without sacrificing quality. Present strategic findings, performance outcomes, and recommendations to clients and internal stakeholders with clarity and authority. Mentor junior strategists by modeling analytical depth, structured thinking, and professional communication. Maintain alignment between video initiatives and larger digital marketing and business KPIs. You Might Be a Fit If You… Are energized by solving complex problems through data and clear frameworks. Can watch a video, explain why it held attention at 0:45 and lost it at 2:10, and fix it in the next brief. Value both autonomy and structured collaboration. You're comfortable leading your own work while integrating effectively within cross-functional teams. Enjoy communicating insights backed by evidence and logic, helping others understand the "why" behind each strategy. Thrive in environments that balance creative thinking with analytical precision. Prefer clarity, process, and repeatable systems over guesswork or improvisation. Take pride in refining strategies through iteration and measurement. Required Experience 5+ years in YouTube strategy, video content strategy, or channel growth. B2B or SaaS experience strongly preferred. Proven success growing YouTube channels or video programs that achieve measurable business outcomes. Advanced analytical and reporting skills (e.g., YouTube Studio, VidIQ or TubeBuddy, Google Analytics, Google Search Console, Ahrefs, HubSpot). Familiarity with AI visibility platforms such as Profound is a plus. Experience managing video production ecosystems: scripting, creators, editors, and outside production partners. Metrics/KPIs Achievement rate of channel-related KPIs (watch time, click-through rate, retention, subscriber growth). Growth in qualified traffic, pipeline, and conversions tied to video initiatives. Strategic deliverables delivered on time and to spec. Client satisfaction with clarity and usefulness of strategy. Efficiency gains through improved systems, playbooks, and AI-assisted workflows. input.description: Director, Content Accessibility College Board – Learning & Assessment Location: This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes. Role Type : This is a full-time position About the Team The Content Accessibility team at College Board has the privilege and responsibility of ensuring that College Board assessments are accessible for individuals with disabilities. Our work is both specialized and broad: we work with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to write and review image descriptions, consult with technology teams to improve accessibility supports in authoring tools, and collaborate with accessibility and accommodations specialists across the organization to ensure test content meets policy and the needs of test-takers. We not only advocate for universal design, we live it. About the Opportunity As a Director, Content Accessibility, you coach a team of writers and reviewers who bridge the gap between students who use assistive technology to take College Board assessments and the makers of College Board assessments. By bridging that gap, your team ensures every test question meets accessibility guidelines. Your attitude is can-do: you write and review image descriptions and evaluate caption tracks, you construct reader scripts and braille maps, you apply headings when the content requires them. Moreover, you take on the team’s most complex and high-stakes work yourself. You do the work because leading by example helps the team excel. Ultimately, in Content Accessibility, everything you do is focused on one goal: ensuring College Board assessments are accessible so that all students, no matter their ability, can show what they know and can do. You can say with confidence that the work of your team is a primary reason College Board is an industry leader in accessible testing. In this role, you will: Lead and develop a team (30%) Lead a team of four specialists responsible for the accessibility of assessment content across all College Board assessments. Own day-to-day direction for the team. Assign and balance workloads, set priorities across competing program deadlines, and adjust plans as schedules shift, in partnership with the Senior Director and program leads. Track and manage progress to goals, and provide coaching and support to ensure team members meet and exceed goals, remain engaged, and contribute meaningfully to our mission. Cultivate an inclusive and high achieving culture that enables all team members to live out College Board ’s Operating Principles. Embody College Board ’s Manager Expectations in your work. Participate in hiring, onboarding, and training, and help shape team roles and structure as needs evolve. Conduct regular check-ins and reviews and coach team members through feedback, professional development plans, and stretch assignments. Be an expert practitioner (40%) Write accessible test content (including image descriptions, reader scripts, and braille transcription notes), maintaining the highest standards of quality and care, for College Board assessments. Personally adopt the hardest cases for yourself. Review and remediate test content to conform to Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), ensuring all tests meet Section 504 and Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements. Adapt strategically when content and standards don’t easily align. Act as the team's authority on accessible-content standards, making final calls on edge cases when guidance is unclear or absent. Review and remediate test-adjacent content (e.g., research studies, scoring guidelines) to conform to WCAG, ensuring all publications meet Section 504 and ADA requirements. Set priorities for and maintain image description guidelines, authoring standards and practices (e.g., for mode transformations), documentation, presentations, and tools (e.g., user personas). Lead quality-control, accessibility, and usability reviews of tests and applications, identifying patterns and root causes rather than one-off errors. Maintain advanced proficiency in authoring tools and assistive technology, and advise the team on best practices. Shape strategy, standards, and cross-functional practice (30%) Contribute to Content Accessibility strategy and long-term planning as part of the team's leadership group, and lead execution of initiatives within your team's scope. Synthesize accessibility research, web standards, and user-experience findings into clear evidence-based recommendations to improve tooling, processes, and authoring standards. Present and advocate for those recommendations to program and organization leadership. Represent Content Accessibility, including the team’s aims, standards, constraints, and risk considerations, in planning conversations with program, product, and technology teams. Ensure accessibility is built into all processes, tools, and assessments. Educate and mentor others about universal design, accessibility, and accommodations, such as through presentations and trainings. Drive pilots of new tools, workflows, and technologies (including AI) that improve the quality, efficiency, or accessibility of test content. Lead cross-team projects or serve on them as the accessibility subject matter expert. About You To qualify for this role, you must have: 6+ years of experience in accessibility or accommodations-focused roles, technical writing, or assessment content writing, with at least 4 years specifically in accessibility or accommodations-related work (e.g., accessibility specialist, inclusive designer, Section 508 compliance analyst) Experience leading people or work, such as supervising, mentoring, training, or leading projects. Excellent written communication skills, with demonstrated experience writing or editing (e.g., technical writer or editor). A strategic and inclusive leadership style: you set clear priorities, build effective team structures, plan for future needs, and foster a culture of belonging. A proven ability to drive performance and growth: you set high expectations, deliver real-time, evidence-based feedback, and coach team members to take smart risks, stretch their skills, and achieve meaningful impact. Excellent verbal communication skills, including facilitating meetings and presenting remotely and in-person to leaders and cross-functional audiences. Demonstrated success handling complex, ambiguous, or high-stakes work with sound judgment and autonomy. Adept problem-solving skills, including using data to inform decisions and actions. Proven ability to build relationships and influence others to action. Experience creating or maintaining accessibility standards or guidelines. Fluency in web-content accessibility (WCAG, ARIA) and/or universal design. Strong organization and prioritization skills and the proven ability to move forward multiple projects in concert, both independently and as a member of the team Outstanding curiosity about emerging trends and best practices in web standards and accessibility Certified Professional in Accessibility Core Competencies (CPACC) certification or Web Accessibility Specialist (WAS) certification preferred Bachelor’s degree required The ability to travel 1–3 times a year to College Board offices or on behalf of College Board business All roles at College Board require: A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively. Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input. A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking. A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success Authorization to work in the United States About Our Process Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days. While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks. What We Offer At College Board , we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market. A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation The hiring range for this role is $80,000 –$135,000. Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board . We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data. We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live. You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more. Remote Originally posted on Himalayas

The Head is accountable for the full events and corporate travel portfolio, consolidated budgets, strategic supplier agreements, service standards, and duty-of-care governance. Serving both internal teams and external stakeholders (clients, prospects, and partners), the Head sets priorities, builds team capability, and manages major commercial decisions and C-level/client escalations. Financial oversight is supported by the Event & Travel Finance Lead in alignment with central Corporate FP&A. A key initial priority is leading the implementation and transition to our enhanced travel operating model. Once established, the Head provides oversight through periodic performance reviews and exception management, delegating routine operations to the team and Travel Management Companies (TMCs). Responsibilities Function Leadership: Lead and develop the Team. Recruit open roles, establish team cadence, and build capabilities across the function. Strategic resource planning across agencies, production vendors, and internal talent to execute both internal and client-facing events seamlessly. Flagship, VIP & Client/client’s customers-Facing Events: Execute on objectives, budgets, and brand standards set by C-Level leadership for 5,000-attendee conference, VIP executive receptions, and regional customer summits. Manage delivery through the internal Team, supported by event specialists and external agencies. Lead venue selection, production, security, contract negotiations, and attendee experience for both internal and external audiences. Internal Meetings & Offsites: Oversee the internal gathering strategy and delivery. Standardize playbooks for routine company meetings and regional leadership offsites. Travel Operating Model Transition: Lead the implementation of our approved global travel operating model, including RFPs and contracts for multi-region TMCs, unified policy and expense frameworks, approvals, reconciliation, and dual quoting. Coordinate phased migration corridor-by-corridor, validate vendor acceptance, protect service continuity, and establish an operational handover once stable. input.title: Founding Creative Director, Interactive & AI

organization.name: Lynton
organization.notes: Company website not supplied. Links open the source listing; confirm all requirements with the employer.

input.description: About Lynton Lynton spent 16 years as a HubSpot partner, delivering 2,000+ projects across 50+ industries. We know SaaS and agency work from the inside. When we saw what was coming with AI, we left HubSpot to build what comes next. We build and run AI-native growth systems for mid-market companies: websites built to be measured, an open-source stack that replaces legacy software, and AI agents that run marketing, sales, and operations. The client owns the infrastructure, we operate the agents, and the whole system has to show what it produces in revenue. If this role sounds like a perfect fit for you, skip ahead to apply directly on our website. We prioritize candidates who apply directly on our site. The opportunity Most agencies have added AI to their production line and kept the creative process they had ten years ago. We started over. AI coding agents build our websites. Our imagery comes from image and video models we direct. The interactive work that used to need a studio and a six-figure budget is now something a small team can ship in weeks. What that makes possible depends on taste. Anyone can generate a thousand images. Very few people can pick the right one, fix what's wrong with it, and make it move in a way that serves the page's argument. That's the job. As our founding creative director, you own the creative and communication strategy for every website and campaign Lynton ships, both ours and our clients'. You decide what a page says and how it looks. You design how it moves. You make or direct every image, illustration, animation, and film on it. Some weeks you're writing the headline. Other weeks you're lighting a scene in Blender, or telling a client their brand deserves better than stock photography. The agency is one part of what we're building. Lynton is also a launchpad for new products, services, and companies we incubate from inside, and with your help we'll take each of them to market. What you'll own Creative and communication strategy. Own the messaging and visual system for every site and campaign. That covers positioning, page structure, headlines, body copy, the design language, and the design tokens that encode it. You write copy yourself and edit everything that ships, so the words and pictures come from one point of view. Interactive experience design. Design how every page moves and responds, including SVG and CSS animation, scroll-driven storytelling, micro-interactions, and real-time 3D. You storyboard it, prototype it, and direct the build. When getting into the timeline yourself is faster than explaining, you do that. 3D and real-time scenes. Model, light, and art-direct scenes in Blender, then bring them to the browser with Three.js and WebGL. You set the bar for when a page earns real-time 3D and when a lighter technique tells the story better. Generated photography and illustration. Build and run the image pipeline. You'll art-direct photography and illustration with image models, keep one style consistent across a whole site or campaign, and retouch what the model gets wrong. You'll also animate stills with video models. You set the house rules on style, consistency, and licensing. Video and motion graphics. Produce product films, launch and explainer videos, social cuts, and motion graphics. Use generative video, compositing, and traditional motion tools in whatever mix gets the best result. Campaign creative. Own launches and email campaigns end to end: concept, copy, landing pages, imagery, and video. A campaign should read as one idea from the inbox to the page. New products, services, and brands. Lead the creative for every launch we incubate: the name and identity, the positioning and story, and the site and campaign it goes to market with. Creative oversight on every engagement. You review and sign off on all creative the agency ships. You're the reason a Lynton site looks and reads like one, and the reason no client site looks like a template. Performance and accessibility as part of the craft. We hold every page to a mobile Lighthouse score of 90 or above and to WCAG AA contrast. Motion respects reduced-motion settings. 3D loads after the headline, so it never delays the first thing a visitor reads. Copy lives in the page, where both people and AI assistants can read it. AI-first production. Direct our agent fleet through the production work: coding agents for prototypes and builds, image and video models for assets, and language models for first drafts and variants. Manage each engagement's inference and render budget like any other resource. Build reusable pipelines so every project starts further ahead than the last. Who you are 8+ years in digital creative, with at least three leading it. You've been a creative director, associate CD, or design lead at an interactive studio, an agency, or an in-house brand team. You've answered for the work across many projects at once. A portfolio of interactive work you directed and helped build. Your sites use motion to carry the story rather than to decorate it. Awards are nice. Work we can click through and feel is what counts. You write. You can turn a positioning brief into a homepage headline and the three paragraphs under it. You can edit someone else's copy until it sounds like a person. To you, words and pictures are one job. Hands-on across the motion stack. You're fluent in CSS and SVG animation, GSAP or an equivalent, and scroll-driven sequencing. You've shipped real-time 3D in the browser with Three.js, React Three Fiber, or similar, and built or lit scenes in Blender, Cinema 4D, or Houdini. You don't need to be the strongest engineer in the room, but you can read the code, prototype with a coding agent, and tell when a build is wrong. Deep, current practice with image and video models. You use them every day and have opinions about which to use for what. You know how to keep a character, a product, or an illustration style consistent across dozens of outputs. You also know where the models still fail. Motion and video craft. You can cut a film, design motion graphics, and finish in After Effects, Premiere, DaVinci Resolve, or their equivalents, alongside generative tools. Taste you can explain. You can say why a typeface, a cut, or a camera move is right, in terms a client or an engineer can act on. Honest with the medium. You'd never present a generated person as a real customer. You know the commercial terms of the models you use. You'd rather ship an honest illustration than a misleading photograph. Performance-minded. You've traded a heavier scene for a faster page and can explain the call. Texture budgets, draw calls, and Core Web Vitals are part of your craft vocabulary. AI-first in practice. You already direct agents across design, code, and copy. You can spec a task, judge the output, and improve the loop. For you, directing agents is the appeal rather than the threat. Ready to build. You're comfortable with a blank page, a small team, and a leadership group that builds alongside you. Bonus Shaders, GLSL, or generative art Rive, Lottie, or Spline for lightweight interactive motion Sound design for web and film Brand identity systems built from scratch Training or fine-tuning image models on a brand's style B2B or professional-services clients Why this role Ground floor with credibility. We have 27 years in business, 16 years of enterprise relationships, and a client base that generates revenue. You'll build the creative function of a new kind of agency on a real foundation. The whole creative surface. Strategy, words, design, interaction, 3D, image, and video all sit with one person. There's no handoff between a copy team, a design team, and a motion vendor. The new tools are the daily workflow here. The models and agents most studios are still piloting are a budget line and an everyday habit at Lynton . Direct to leadership. You work directly with the CMO and the founder, with no creative committee in between, and your work ships to real clients. Originally posted on Himalayas

input.title: Content Writer

organization.name: EnerVenue, Inc.
organization.notes: Company website not supplied. Links open the source listing; confirm all requirements with the employer.

input.description: About EnerVenue EnerVenue is an energy infrastructure company commercializing the Aqueous Metal Cell (AMC), a nickel-hydrogen battery built on the chemistry NASA developed for the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station. Founded in 2020 by Stanford professor Yi Cui, the company has adapted that aerospace chemistry for grid-scale storage on Earth: an aqueous cell with no lithium and no rare earths, designed for 30,000 cycles and a 30-year design life, with zero risk of fire from thermal runaway. Research and development is based in Fremont, California, commercial operations run from Hong Kong and Singapore, and manufacturing is in Changzhou, Jiangsu. In March 2026 EnerVenue closed a $300 million Series B extension, taking total funding to over $700 million. A high-volume manufacturing line is under construction in Changzhou, targeting 250 MWh of annual capacity in Q3 2026 and scaling toward 1 GWh in 2027. EnerVenue ranked second worldwide in energy storage and distribution in the 2025 TIME and Statista Top GreenTech Companies list, and was named to the list for a third consecutive year in 2026. The Role EnerVenue is looking for a Content Writer to produce the content that carries the company's argument to utilities, developers, data-center operators, investors and regulators across multiple platforms and publishing outlets. This is the first dedicated content hire in the communications function, and it reports to the Head of Communications. The work is writing, not coordination. EnerVenue is not marketing a better battery, it is establishing long-duration storage as permanent infrastructure, and that case is made in arguments that earn attention on their own merits: research pieces for the industry hub, bylined articles placed in trade and mainstream energy press, white papers written for the people who sign off on capital, and a company page that looks outward at the sector rather than inward at its own announcements. The successful candidate can hold an argument together across 2,000 words and across 200 characters, and can do both in the same week. The function runs to a documented editorial standard: locked product and safety language, a claim discipline in which every statistic is traced to a named primary source and verified before publication, and a house style that rejects marketing register. Anyone who has worked in a newsroom will recognize the discipline, and will find the freedom that comes with it. The argument is yours to make. The wording of a safety or performance claim is not, and that boundary is what makes the work publishable. Key Responsibilities Thought Leadership and Long-Form Content Write the deep, top-of-funnel pieces that anchor the content program: industry research articles, executive white papers, procurement and due-diligence guides, sector playbooks (data centers, utilities, mining, ports, telecom) and technical deep dives Write bylined articles for placement in trade and mainstream energy press, in the voice of the assigned spokesperson, working from documented voice specifications rather than guesswork Build each piece to the house architecture: one reframe, an evidence spine, third-party authority at the open and the close, a single late company insertion, and a close that argues the category rather than the product Source every figure to a named primary with its date cited in the draft, verify it before publication, and write it back into the evidence library so the corpus compounds instead of the number being used once and lost Work the idea bank and the live content territories, and bring your own angles rather than waiting for a brief LinkedIn and Social Produce company-page content across the full format palette: same-week reaction to a dated external development, one-number posts built on a single verified statistic, explainer cards, honest answers to real buyer questions, counterweight posts, polls, documentary place-and-people content, and event content Turn same-week reactions around inside 48 hours. This is the format that decides whether the page reads as a participant in the sector or a broadcaster of its own news Draft executive content within the established persona system for the chief executive, and support additional spokespeople as the roster expands Tag every post by format at publication so performance can be read by shape, and use the monthly analytics review to decide what to make more of and what to retire Support X and the Chinese channel map as those lanes develop Pair every statistic with a chart built on the brand grid. A strong number published without a visual wastes the number Editorial Standards and Claim Discipline Work inside the locked language: canonical product naming (AMC, Energy Rack, Energy Prism, Energy Venue), the canonical safety wording, and the banned-language list Never deploy an unsourced statistic, an ungated claim, or an attack on a named competitor. Route anything new to the Head of Communications before it reaches a draft that leaves the building Distinguish what has been delivered from what has been demonstrated from what is intended, and write each in the register it can carry Hold house style: no buzzwords, no “this is not X, it is Y” constructions, no manufactured urgency, no sales language, no em dashes Production, Agency Interface and Measurement Run the content calendar day to day and keep the pipeline register current, from pitch through greenlight to publication Brief and review the content agency that repurposes long-form pieces into the LinkedIn and newsletter layers, and hold the wording line on what comes back Support press releases, media materials, briefing notes and event content as the news cycle demands Contribute to internal communications, including the internal newsletter Report monthly on content performance by format, channel and audience Required Qualifications Experience Four or more years writing published business, technical or editorial content for a professional audience, with a portfolio that can be read rather than described Experience in the renewables industry is required. Energy storage experience is strongly preferred and will be the deciding factor between otherwise comparable candidates Demonstrable long-form thought leadership: pieces that make an argument and carry evidence, not product marketing dressed as insight Ghostwriting in a named executive voice, with samples and with a clear account of how the voice was built LinkedIn as a primary professional channel, covering both company-page and executive content, with working familiarity with native formats and analytics Social media content production across at least one channel beyond LinkedIn Craft Native-level written English, and a plain, declarative style that does not reach for adjectives to carry an argument The judgment to recognize which claim is defensible and which is not, and the discipline to ask rather than write around it Ability to read primary material (analyst reports, standards documents, regulatory filings, technical datasheets) and extract a figure that will survive scrutiny Comfortable turning engineering substance into language a chief financial officer or a procurement lead will act on, without flattening the engineering Speed under a news cycle, and accuracy under speed Ways of Working Self-directed. This is a small function with no editorial layer between the writer and publication Comfortable working inside a governed, version-controlled knowledge base: markdown, plain-text documents, and a single source of truth for language and claims Reliable across time zones, with working overlap with Changzhou, China and the United States West Coast Willing to travel occasionally for site visits, events and content gathering Preferred Qualifications Direct experience covering or working in long-duration energy storage, grid-scale batteries, grid infrastructure or data-center power Former journalist or trade-press editor, particularly in energy Familiarity with the standards and regulatory landscape that storage content has to respect, including NFPA 855, UL 9540A and UL 1973, interconnection and permitting Search and generative-engine optimization literacy: how content gets found, and how it gets cited by AI answer engines Data-visualization literacy, and the habit of building the chart alongside the copy Agency-side experience, or experience managing an agency relationship from the client side Mandarin Chinese, for the China market lane and for work with the Changzhou team Fluency with AI tools as research and drafting aids inside a claim-discipline framework, and clarity about where their output stops being usable What EnerVenue Offers A category being defined rather than a product being marketed, which is a rare thing for a writer to get access to Direct access to the chief executive and to technical leadership, and content that lands in front of buyers, investors, regulators and the trade press A documented language and evidence framework, so that published work is defensible on the day it appears and does not get relitigated afterwards Competitive compensation A company backed by long-term investors, with a clear path to gigawatt-scale production A mission-driven team building infrastructure designed to last 30 years, not a consumable product Originally posted on Himalayas

Influencer marketing plays an increasingly important role in how we build brand awareness, create authentic storytelling, and engage new audiences. We’re looking for someone who understands creator culture, enjoys building relationships, and thrives in a fast-moving environment where trends, campaigns, and partnerships evolve quickly. The Role We’re looking for an Influencer Marketing Specialist to take full ownership of Seeking’s influencer and creator marketing initiatives, driving partnerships, managing campaigns, and overseeing the day-to-day operations of our influencer marketing efforts. This role will take full ownership of the influencer lifecycle, from sourcing and securing targeted creators to leading negotiations, managing relationships, executing campaigns, coordinating deliverables, and supporting influencer events. This includes overseeing paid and organic UGC initiatives, independently managing the negotiation process from initial outreach through contract execution, and collaborating with talent managers, agencies, photographers, videographers, and internal teams. The ideal candidate is highly organized, proactive, relationship-driven, and passionate about influencer marketing, creator culture, and social media trends. They must be able to take full ownership of initiatives from concept through execution, independently managing timelines, budgets, relationships, and deliverables to ensure successful campaign execution. Why This Hire Matters Influencer marketing is one of the most important and effective parts of our marketing strategy, offering an authentic way to connect with consumers and drive brand discovery. With the largest budget within the Marketing Department, this role plays a critical part in driving business growth and maximizing return on investment. This position will lead efforts to scale our influencer marketing program by building long-term creator partnerships, executing impactful campaigns, supporting experiential activations, and ensuring every partnership delivers measurable business value. As a brand that operates in a sometimes controversial space, we need someone who is comfortable navigating public perceptions, understands the challenges and opportunities that come with marketing a polarizing brand, and can confidently identify, pitch, and secure creators who align with our positioning. The ideal candidate will approach these challenges strategically and creatively, turning potential barriers into opportunities for meaningful partnerships and brand growth. What You’ll Own Influencer Recruitment & Relationship Management Own the end-to-end influencer recruitment process, from identifying and evaluating creators to negotiating and securing partnerships and managing long-term relationships. Independently source, vet, and recruit influencers, UGC creators, ambassadors, and content partners across TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Pinterest and emerging platforms. Build and manage a strong pipeline of influencers and UGC creators aligned with Seeking's brand, target audiences, and marketing objectives. Lead influencer outreach, briefs, pitches, relationship development, and partnership negotiations. Identify and secure high-value brand aligned creators in all tiers, including emerging talent, established influencers, and larger-scale personalities. Develop long-term creator partnerships that extend beyond individual campaigns and support ongoing brand initiatives. Manage multiple influencer campaigns simultaneously, ensuring deadlines, deliverables, budgets, and quality expectations are met. Oversee creator content development, feedback, approvals, posting schedules, and campaign execution. Proactively identify and resolve campaign challenges without requiring constant oversight. Ensure influencer campaigns are aligned with Seeking's brand positioning, creative direction, and marketing priorities. Take accountability for campaign execution and performance, identifying opportunities to improve results. Manage campaign timelines and project schedules. Influencer Partnerships, Negotiations & Agency Management Lead negotiations with influencers, talent managers, and agencies to secure competitive rates and favorable partnership terms. Own day-to-day relationships with influencer agencies and talent management partners. Evaluate creator proposals, partnership opportunities, pricing, and anticipated value. Negotiate content deliverables, exclusivity, usage rights, licensing, and partnership terms in collaboration with appropriate internal teams. Manage agency performance, ensuring external partners deliver against campaign objectives, budgets, and timelines. Identify opportunities to negotiate more efficient deals, establish recurring partnerships, and maximize the value of influencer investments. Build strong industry relationships and proactively bring new talent and partnership opportunities to Seeking. Influencer Budgets, Contracts & Operations Manage allocated influencer marketing budgets, ensuring campaigns are executed efficiently and within approved spending limits. Evaluate creator pricing, negotiate costs, and recommend how to allocate budgets across partnerships. Oversee the influencer contracting process in collaboration with internal stakeholders and legal partners. Manage partnership agreements, payment schedules, invoices, usage rights, and licensing documentation. Own and continuously improve influencer databases, campaign tracking systems, and creator relationship management processes. Develop efficient workflows for creator outreach, onboarding, campaign execution, reporting, and renewals. Maintain clear visibility into active partnerships, financial commitments, deliverables, and campaign status. Creating and maintaining documented processes and workflows Social Productions, Activations & Events Support the planning and execution of influencer events, brand activations, experiential campaigns, pop-ups, and creator experiences. Coordinate influencer attendance and travel logistics when applicable. Manage creator itineraries for events and productions. Coordinate creators, agencies, vendors, and internal teams. Coordinate creator content collection following campaigns and events. Ensure influencer deliverables are received, approved, and archived. Content, Creative Collaboration & Cultural Trends Proactively develop influencer content ideas, creator collaborations, and campaign concepts that align with Seeking's brand identity. Stay deeply connected to influencer culture, emerging creators, internet trends, and evolving social media platforms. Identify timely cultural moments and partnership opportunities where Seeking can participate in relevant conversations. Work with creators to develop authentic, engaging content while maintaining brand messaging and creative expectations. Collaborate with Creative, Social Media, PR, and Brand teams to integrate influencer partnerships into larger campaigns. Recommend innovative influencer formats, content approaches, and creator-led initiatives that differentiate Seeking. Identify opportunities to repurpose high-performing influencer content across paid media, organic social, PR, and other marketing channels, subject to secured usage rights. Performance Reporting & Optimization Own performance tracking and reporting for influencer marketing campaigns and partnerships. Establish and monitor campaign KPIs, including reach, engagement, impressions, traffic, conversions, and cost efficiency. Evaluate creator performance to determine which partnerships should be continued, expanded, renegotiated, or discontinued. Analyze campaign results and translate performance insights into actionable recommendations. Identify opportunities to improve creator selection, partnership costs, content performance, and overall influencer ROI. Present recurring performance updates, campaign insights, and recommendations to marketing leadership. Continuously test new influencer approaches, creator categories, and partnership formats to improve results. Cross-Functional Leadership & Collaboration Serve as the primary owner of influencer marketing execution across Seeking's marketing initiatives. Lead influencer-related workstreams and hold internal and external stakeholders accountable for agreed deliverables and timelines. About You This section matters just as much as your experience. We’re hiring for someone who understands creator culture and enjoys building relationships. Experience with paid social advertising, particularly Meta Ads Manager and TikTok Ads Manager, and an understanding of how influencer-generated content can support paid acquisition. Experience with creator whitelisting, partnership ads, and paid amplification of influencer content. input.description: What You’ll Do You’ll own the social media engine that accelerates Prep Network ’s subscription success — shaping how we speak, publish, and show up across all channels. You’ll guide the daily output for Prep Network 's subscription brands, support new initiatives like Prep Scores, and collaborate with our event marketing team to maximize reach, strengthen storytelling, and drive meaningful growth. You’ll build and manage the full social calendar for our digital brands, publish a high volume of engaging content highlighting our articles, rankings, features, and recruiting guidance. You’ll partner closely with video and graphics teams to turn ideas into scroll-stopping assets, and you’ll guide our digital social contributors and VAs with clear briefs, expectations, and posting standards. Who We Are Prep Network is a sports company that connects high school athletes with college coaches. Through our nine brands, we publish over 4,000 articles each month and actively scout talented athletes across the U.S. We aim to discover and promote promising prospects who aspire to play at the collegiate level. In addition to our content, Prep Network is the top event operator in the U.S., hosting 200+ tournaments annually. We offer a combination of top-tier competitions and extensive media exposure for attending teams. Our 250+ showcases each year provide a platform for over 10,000+ prospects to compete in front of colleges, scouts, and media outlets. We’re pumped to have been named one of the "Best Places to Work" by Minneapolis/St. Paul Business Journal for five years running, and to land a spot on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list of America’s fastest-growing private companies. Prep Network isn’t your average sports company; we’re all about helping student-athletes succeed and creating an awesome workplace. Core Responsibilities Plans and Publishes the Daily Content Calendar Across All Brands: builds and runs the weekly calendar for multiple social channels across all brands, building brand awareness and promoting articles, ranking drops, recruiting and commitment news, scores and subscription features, engagement posts, and product updates. Sets and Executes Brand Voice and Community Engagement Across Channels: writes copy in each brand’s voice, defines tone and engagement standards, models them in day-to-day community engagement responding to comments and messages, and reviews team content for quality and consistency. Shapes Briefs and Leads Asset Production with Video and Graphics Teams: writes creative briefs, sets priorities and deadlines, and makes sure assets are ready ahead of publishing and events. Manages Digital Social Contributors, VAs and the Coordinator: recruits, trains, assigns work and holds the team accountable for output and quality. Owns Performance Reporting and Leads Campaigns with Cross-Team Partners: tracks and reports social metrics, uses the data to adjust strategy, and executes subscription and marketing campaigns with other departments. Must-Haves in a Candidate Social Media Mastery: 2-3 years in social media strategy and execution for multi-brand or content-driven organizations. Platform Fluency: Deep understanding of Instagram, TikTok, X/Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, Threads, and emerging platforms. Creative & Analytical Balance: Strong copywriting and creative instinct, paired with comfort in reading performance data to iterate. Team Leadership: Experience overseeing part-time social media contributors, freelancers, or agencies. Brand Voice Stewardship: Ability to craft and sustain a recognizable brand identity through content. Collaboration: Works seamlessly across departments — digital, video, graphics, events, and marketing. Nice-to-Haves in a Candidate Social Listening: Proven ability to identify early platform trends and pivot content strategy quickly. Multi-Brand Navigation: Experience toggling between multiple voices or sub-brands without sacrificing consistency or clarity. Tool Proficiency: Knowledgeable in platforms such as Sprout Social (or a similar social media management tool), Asana, Google Workspace, and Slack. Sports Industry Insight: Brings experience or strong familiarity with youth athletics or sports media, enhancing relevance and brand alignment. SEO & Social Search Knowledge: Understands how social algorithms index content and can optimize titles, captions, keywords, and thumbnails for discovery. Educational Background – A Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, or a related field is preferred. Work Eligibility Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future visa sponsorship. Only U.S. citizens will be considered for this role at this time. Benefits and Perks At Prep Network , we take pride in our culture and commitment to creating an exceptional workplace environment. Here are some of the benefits and perks you can expect when you join our team: Vibrant Culture. Prep Network has been recognized as one of the Best Places to Work for five years running, thanks to our vibrant and inclusive culture. We’re passionate about bringing on board curious, self-motivated individuals who work hard and genuinely enjoy their work. Autonomy. We trust our team members to excel in their roles. Rather than micromanaging, we provide you with the tools and processes needed for success, allowing you the freedom to bring your role to life and make a meaningful impact. Professional Growth. We prioritize your professional development. We actively support and encourage you to invest in your personal and professional growth. Comprehensive Benefits. We offer comprehensive health benefits, a 401(k) with Safe Harbor matching, long-term disability, and Basic Life Insurance. Work arrangements are flexible; whether you're in our Plymouth, MN office or working remotely from your home, we trust you to do great work from wherever you do it best. Competitive Compensation. Targeted salary is $60,000 - $65,000. The starting salary will depend on the skills and applicable experience you bring to this role. Prep Network 's success is driven by its people. By hiring and supporting A-players, you will directly influence the experience of thousands of athletes and coaches we serve annually. Join our dynamic team, where we value your individuality, foster professional growth, and provide a diverse range of benefits. Discover a workplace where you can thrive, learn, and make a meaningful impact on our shared journey. Originally posted on Himalayas

input.description: Availity delivers revenue cycle and related business solutions for health care professionals who want to build healthy, thriving organizations. Availity has the powerful tools, actionable insights and expansive network reach that medical businesses need to get an edge in an industry constantly redefined by change. At Availity , we're not just another Healthcare Technology company; we're pioneers reshaping the future of healthcare! With our headquarters in vibrant Jacksonville, FL, and an exciting office in Bangalore, India, along with an exceptional remote workforce across the United States, we're a global team united by a powerful mission. We're on a mission to bring the focus back to what truly matters - patient care. As the leading healthcare engagement platform, we're the heartbeat of an industry that impacts millions. With over 3 million providers connected to health plans, and processing over 19 billion transactions annually, our influence is continually expanding. Join our energetic, dynamic, and forward-thinking team where your ideas are celebrated, innovation is encouraged, and every contribution counts. We're transforming the healthcare landscape, solving communication challenges, and creating connections that empower the nation's premier healthcare ecosystem. The Program Manager, Product supports the Product organization by driving the planning, coordination, and execution of cross-functional product initiatives. This role partners closely with Product Managers, Engineering, Design, Data, Operations, and other teams to ensure product programs progress efficiently from planning through launch. The Program Manager brings structure and visibility to complex initiatives, manages timelines and dependencies, identifies risks and blockers, and facilitates effective communication across teams. This role is an individual contributor position that requires strong collaboration, organization, problem-solving, and the ability to influence outcomes without direct authority. The ideal candidate is comfortable operating in a fast-paced product environment, managing multiple priorities, and bringing clarity to ambiguous or complex problems. To be qualified for the role, you have: Required Bachelor’s degree in Business, Product Management, Operations, Technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. 3–5 years of experience in program management, project management, product operations, product management, or a related field. Experience working in a technology, software, or other product-driven environment. Experience working in a regulated industry such as healthcare or financial services. Healthcare background is highly preferred. Demonstrated ability to coordinate cross-functional initiatives involving multiple teams. Strong organizational and time-management skills. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment. Ability to influence and coordinate stakeholders without direct authority. Proficiency with common project management, collaboration, and productivity tools. Preferred Experience working directly with Product and Engineering teams. Familiarity with Agile/Scrum product development methodologies. Experience supporting software or digital product launches. Experience with product roadmap planning and prioritization processes. Familiarity with tools such as Jira, Confluence, Asana, Monday.com, Smartsheet, or similar platforms. Core Competencies Execution: Consistently drives assigned initiatives forward and delivers against commitments. Organization: Creates structure, maintains accurate documentation, and effectively manages competing priorities. Collaboration: Builds productive relationships across Product and partner functions. Communication: Clearly communicates status, risks, decisions, and next steps. Problem Solving: Identifies issues and develops practical solutions. Influence: Gains alignment and drives accountability without formal authority. Adaptability: Effectively navigates changing priorities and ambiguity. Product Orientation: Understands the connection between customer needs, product priorities, technology, and business outcomes. What you will be doing: Program Management Manage the day-to-day execution of assigned product programs and initiatives. Develop and maintain program plans, timelines, milestones, deliverables, and dependencies. Coordinate activities across Product, Engineering, Design, Data, Operations, and other stakeholder teams. Track progress against commitments and proactively identify potential delays or issues. Maintain clear documentation and visibility into program status. Ensure action items, decisions, and follow-ups are clearly documented and completed. Cross-Functional Collaboration Partner with Product Managers and functional leads to coordinate execution of product initiatives. Facilitate working sessions, planning meetings, status meetings, and project reviews. Build alignment across teams with shared goals and interdependent deliverables. Follow up on commitments and help teams resolve execution issues. Serve as a central point of coordination for assigned programs. Product Development & Launch Support product initiatives across discovery, planning, development, testing, launch, and post-launch activities. Coordinate launch readiness activities across relevant Product and business teams. Track key launch dependencies and ensure outstanding items are identified and addressed. Support development of launch plans, timelines, communications, and readiness checklists. Help coordinate post-launch activities and follow-up actions. Risk & Dependency Management Identify risks, issues, dependencies, and resource constraints that may affect program delivery. Work with stakeholders to develop mitigation plans and resolve blockers. Escalate significant issues when additional support or decision-making is required. Maintain program-level risk and dependency tracking. Provide timely visibility into changes that may impact scope, schedule, or deliverables. Product Planning & Operations Support quarterly and annual product planning activities. Help maintain visibility into roadmap initiatives, milestones, dependencies, and priorities. Support Product leadership and Product Managers with planning materials, reporting, and operational processes. Develop and maintain dashboards, status reports, and other program-management artifacts. Identify opportunities to improve product planning and execution processes. Contribute to the development and adoption of consistent Product operating practices. Communication & Reporting Provide clear and concise program updates to Product and cross-functional stakeholders. Prepare status reports, presentations, dashboards, and other program communications. Communicate changes to timelines, scope, risks, and dependencies in a timely manner. Ensure stakeholders understand decisions, responsibilities, and next steps. Availity culture and benefits: Availity is a certified "Great Place to Work"! Culture is important to us and there are many ways for you to make your mark here! We have several Culture teams, a Young Professionals Group, and various ways to engage with fellow Availity associates – if you’re near Jacksonville, we have lots of pop up lunches where lunch is provided for everyone when we can see meetings are taking place and we’ve got teams in the office. Availity is a culture of continuous learning. We have many resources and experts in our tech stack, our industry and your function that can help get you there too! We offer a competitive salary, bonus structure, generous HSA company contribution, healthcare, vision, dental benefits and a 401k match program that you can take advantage of on day one! We offer unlimited PTO for salaried associates + 9 paid holidays. Hourly associates start at 19 days of PTO and go up from there with all the same holiday benefits. Interested in wellness? We allow our associates to reimburse up to $250/year for gym memberships, participation in racing events, weight management programs, etc. Interested in furthering your education? We offer education reimbursement! Availity offers Paid Parental Leave for both moms and dads, both birth parents and adoptive parents. Want to work for an organization that gives back to the community? You're at the right place! Availity partners with various organizations, both locally and nationally, to raise awareness, funds and morale as our staff members volunteer their time and funds to engage the organizations campaign. Next steps: After you apply, you will receive text/email messages thanking you for applying and then you will continue to receive more text/email messages alerting you as to where you are in the recruitment process. Interview process: Recruiter Recorded Video Pre-Screen Interview with Product Manager Interview with VP Product Management Video Camera Usage: Availity fosters a collaborative and open culture where communication and engagement are central to our success. As a remote first company, we are also camera-first and provide all associates with camera/video capability to simulate the office environment. If you are not able to use your camera for all virtual meetings, you should not apply for this role. Having cameras on helps create a more connected, interactive, and productive environment, allowing teams to communicate more effectively and build stronger working relationships. The usage of cameras also enhances security and protects sensitive company information. Video participation is required to ensure that only authorized personnel are present in meetings and to prevent unauthorized access, data breaches, preventing social engineering, or the sharing of confidential information with non-participants. Disclaimers: Availity is an equal opportunity employer and makes decisions in employment matters without regard to race, religious creed, color, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, national origin, religion, marital status, medical condition, disability, military service, pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions, or any other classification protected by federal, state, and local laws and ordinances. Availity is a drug-free workplace. Candidates are required to pass a drug test before beginning employment. NOTICE: Federal law requires all employers to verify the identity and employment eligibility of all persons hired to work in the United States. When required by state law or federal regulation, Availity uses I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification in conjunction with E-Verify to determine employment eligibility.
