Depending on client needs, support hands-on content creation, including photography, video capture and editing, real-time content production, and occasional attendance at events or appearances. Branded Content & Partnership Support Support the planning and execution of social media content associated with the client's endorsement agreements and commercial partnerships. Collaborate with Allied Sports' Talent Representation team, brand partners, and external agencies to coordinate content concepts, timelines, and deliverables. Assist with branded content development, including creative concepts, scripts, shot lists, and content recommendations. Community Management & Performance Reporting Monitor social media engagement, audience sentiment, and relevant conversations across platforms. Identify opportunities for audience interaction, community growth, and increased engagement. Track key social media performance metrics, including audience growth, reach, engagement, and content performance. Prepare monthly performance reports highlighting key metrics, content insights, and recommendations for improvement. Stay informed on emerging social media platforms, trends, tools, and best practices within sports, entertainment, and digital culture. Qualifications & Experience 3–5 years of professional experience in social media management, digital content, influencer marketing, or a related field. Demonstrated experience managing social media accounts, developing content calendars, and supporting audience growth and engagement. Experience working with professional athletes, high-profile talent, influencers, or public figures preferred. Strong understanding of Instagram, TikTok, X, and emerging social media platforms, including content trends, analytics, and best practices. Familiarity with content creation and editing tools such as CapCut, Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, or similar platforms. Strong creative instincts and the ability to develop engaging, platform-appropriate content ideas. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to adapt content to reflect an individual's voice and personality. Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Proactive, resourceful, and comfortable working independently while collaborating with internal and external stakeholders. Strong interest in sports, entertainment, pop culture, and the evolving digital media landscape. Ability to exercise professionalism, discretion, and confidentiality when working with high-profile individuals. Flexibility to accommodate occasional evening, weekend, or event-related needs based on business requirements. Position Details This is a remote, temporary, part-time position supporting one designated client within Allied Sports' Talent Representation division. The position is anticipated to require approximately 20–30 hours per week, with flexibility based on client needs and business priorities. The initial assignment is expected to last approximately 90 days, with the possibility of extension based on performance, client needs, and evolving business requirements. The Social Media Manager will report to the VP, Partnership Development and collaborate directly with the client and Allied Sports' Talent Representation team. Occasional travel, event attendance, or hands-on content production may be requested based on client needs. The scope and duration of the position may evolve over time based on business needs and client requirements. Originally posted on Himalayas

input.description: Shipping, Receiving & Production Coordinator We are looking for a highly organized, detail-oriented, and self-motivated Shipping, Receiving & Production Coordinator to join our team. This role is an important link between receiving, production, customer service, vendors, and outbound fulfillment. The ideal candidate is someone who takes pride in accuracy, notices small details, communicates clearly, and is willing to jump in wherever needed to help keep orders moving through the shop. This is also a hands-on physical role. The employee must be able to regularly lift, carry, move, and organize large and heavy boxes and packages in, around, and out of the warehouse on a daily basis. Responsibilities Receiving & Inventory Check-In Receive inbound shipments from vendors, suppliers, and customers. Carry, move, and organize boxes and packages throughout the warehouse and production areas. Individually count merchandise and match items against purchase orders and packing slips. Verify quantities, sizes, colors, styles, product details, and order information. Note and document any discrepancies, damages, shortages, overages, or incorrect items. Communicate with customers and vendors when questions or issues arise. Help resolve receiving issues quickly and accurately. Ensure received merchandise is organized, labeled, and routed to the correct department or staging area. Production Coordination Sort incoming and completed orders and assign them to the correct production department. Update our online production management system, Microsoft Planner, to match purchase order details, order notes, production status, customer requirements, and internal updates. Maintain a general working knowledge of order status, including where jobs are located in the shop, what stage they are in, and whether there are any issues or delays. Help communicate important order details between customer service, receiving, production, and shipping. Follow up internally when orders are missing information, waiting on goods, delayed, or need clarification. Help keep orders moving smoothly through the shop from receiving to production to final fulfillment. Decoration & Production Support Occasional hands-on production support may be required, including: Heat pressing Laser engraving UVDTF application Basic order preparation Applying labels, tags, or finishing touches Other decoration, fulfillment, or production support tasks as needed Outbound Fulfillment & Shipping Separate completed orders as needed. Pack orders carefully, accurately, and professionally. Move packed orders and packages to the correct pickup, shipping, or staging area. Process outbound shipments using UPS WorldShip. Print and apply labels for local pickups, shipments, courier deliveries, and internal order movement. Provide packing dimensions and weights to customers when requested. Arrange local couriers when needed. Ensure completed orders are clearly labeled, organized, and ready for pickup, delivery, or shipment. Help maintain a clean and organized shipping and receiving area. Requirements Must be detail-oriented and highly organized. Must be bilingual. Must be reliable, punctual, and self-motivated. Must be able to work independently and take initiative. Must be comfortable communicating with customers, vendors, and internal team members. Must care about small details, accuracy, and order organization. Must be willing to help other departments when needed. Must be able to regularly lift, carry, move, and organize large and heavy boxes and packages in, around, and out of the warehouse on a daily basis. Must be comfortable working in a warehouse and production environment. Basic computer skills required. Experience with Microsoft Planner, UPS WorldShip, production management software, or shipping/receiving is a plus. Experience in apparel decoration, screen printing, embroidery, promotional products, warehouse operations, or fulfillment is a plus. Ideal Candidate: The right person for this role is someone who enjoys keeping things organized, catching mistakes before they become problems, and helping a busy production shop run smoothly. You should be comfortable switching between computer work, order tracking, warehouse organization, customer/vendor communication, physical inventory handling, and occasional hands-on production support. This is not just a packing or shipping position. This role requires someone who can understand order flow, communicate clearly, track details accurately, and help make sure every job moves through the shop correctly from receiving to final delivery. How to Apply: Please submit your resume along with a brief message about your experience with shipping, receiving, order coordination, production support, warehouse organization, or fulfillment. Experience in apparel decoration, promotional products, or custom production is a plus, but we are willing to train the right person who is organized, dependable, physically capable, and eager to learn. Pay: From $15.00 per hour Work Location: In person

input.description: About WeaponUp WeaponUp is a fast-growing women's wellness company and the creator of The Original Sword Yoga™, a movement practice combining the kung fu straight sword with yoga. Through our online Studio, community, live experiences and events, WeaponUp is building a new approach to movement centered around strength, confidence and grace. Our global community is made up almost entirely of women, and our mission is simple: to create movement experiences that help women feel graceful, empowered, more capable and more at home in their bodies. WeaponUp is a growing, founder-led company based in Florida, with a creative, fast-moving team working across content, community, events, partnerships and digital wellness. As WeaponUp continues to grow, we're looking for a part-time Talent & Production Coordinator to help us identify new talent and coordinate the process of bringing instructors and other movement professionals into the WeaponUp Studio. About the Role This role will work directly with WeaponUp's Founder & CEO and will be responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of our growing talent pipeline. A large part of the role will involve researching and sourcing potential instructors and movement talent, particularly across Florida. You'll identify strong candidates, conduct initial outreach, manage applications and submissions, and organize potential talent for review. Once someone is selected, you'll help manage the operational process of getting them ready for production-from coordinating schedules and agreements to tracking programming and production requirements. The Founder will lead the overall creative direction and make final talent selections. You'll be responsible for the research, coordination and follow-through that keeps the process moving. Responsibilities Research and source potential instructors and movement talent Identify candidates through social media, studios, professional networks, referrals and direct research Review candidate profiles, portfolios, reels and other materials Maintain WeaponUp's talent database and track candidates throughout the process Conduct initial outreach and manage talent communications Manage applications, submissions and follow-ups Coordinate interviews, auditions and meetings Prepare organized candidate shortlists for Founder review Coordinate availability, scheduling and production logistics Track agreements, programming, deadlines and production requirements Communicate with talent before and after production Keep accurate records and ensure next steps are consistently followed Assist with other talent and production-related projects as the Studio grows Who We're Looking For We're looking for a motivated, organized and resourceful person who enjoys finding great people and making projects happen. You should be naturally curious, a strong researcher, comfortable reaching out to new people, and excellent at keeping track of details, deadlines and follow-ups. The right person is proactive and independent-someone who can take direction, understand what we're looking for, and run with it without needing constant oversight. You should have a good eye for talent and on-camera presence and be comfortable working across social media, online research and professional networks to find the right people. Ideally, you have 2-5 years of experience in talent, casting, production, entertainment, creator/influencer management, events, PR or a related field. Experience working with performers, creators or other on-camera talent is a strong plus, as is a background or interest in dance, fitness, movement or performance. Most importantly, we're looking for someone who is reliable, personable, detail-oriented and genuinely excited to take ownership of a growing project. We're looking for someone who is: • Highly organized and detail-oriented • An excellent researcher • Comfortable conducting outreach and building relationships • Able to manage multiple candidates and deadlines simultaneously • Proactive about following up and moving projects forward • Comfortable working independently • Able to take direction and quickly understand what we're looking for • Professional and personable when representing WeaponUp externally You may have previously worked as a Talent Coordinator, Casting Coordinator or Associate, Production Coordinator, Talent Booker, Agency Coordinator, Creator Partnerships Coordinator, or in a similar role. Experience working with performers, creators, instructors, models, athletes or other on-camera talent is strongly preferred. Position Details Type: Part-time independent contractor Compensation: $35/hour Hours: Approximately 20 hours per week Location: Remote; Florida-based candidates preferred Reports to: Founder & CEO Some availability for meetings during normal business hours will be required, and occasional travel or in-person work in Florida may be available as productions grow. To Apply Please submit your resume and a short introduction outlining any relevant experience you've had working with talent, casting, creators, production or entertainment. Experience working within dance, fitness, performance or other movement-based industries is especially encouraged.

input.description: The Role in One Sentence The Producer takes a qualified client opportunity and turns it into a compelling, executable live-event solution that the client wants to buy. Summary You’ll work closely with the Sales and Creative teams to turn client needs and ideas into compelling, executable live-event solutions. Your primary focus will be understanding what the client wants to accomplish, asking the right questions, developing the event approach, bringing together the right internal expertise, and translating the solution into proposals, presentations, and budgets. In this client-facing role, you will be a partner with the production team to ensure continuity between what was envisioned and what is delivered and participating onsite as appropriate. We’re looking for someone who understands live events, enjoys working with clients, and can help turn an opportunity into an experience, with an emphasis on client leadership and solution development rather than detailed day-to-day project management. Key Responsibilities The Producer works across Precon to shape qualified opportunities into compelling, executable live-event solutions. Success in this role requires curiosity, creative thinking, and enough production fluency to connect a client’s goals with what Precon can bring to life. This role leads the thinking and collaboration that moves an opportunity from initial idea, then stays engaged with the production team to ensure what was envisioned is successfully delivered. Client Discovery Partner with Sales on client discovery conversations to understand objectives, audience, priorities, budget, brand, and desired outcomes. Ask thoughtful questions, identify opportunities, and help clients articulate needs they may not yet know how to define. Develop proposals, scopes, budgets, and presentations. Respond thoughtfully to client feedback, questions, and budget considerations. Event Solution & Experience Development Translate client objectives and early ideas into compelling live-event concepts and solutions. Serve as the connective voice across client, creative, technical, and production teams. Help shape how staging, scenic, content, technology, branding, and the physical environment work together to create the desired audience experience. Production Partnership & Onsite Execution Partner with Project Manager, Technical Director, Creative team, and other internal resources. Work with team to key milestones to ensure continuity between what was sold and what is delivered. Participate onsite as appropriate, maintaining client relationships and helping solve creative, production, or experience-related challenges in real time. Support post-event client conversations and identify opportunities to strengthen or expand the relationship. Location & Travel Requirements This is a remote position based in the Washington, DC metropolitan area, with regular in-person client meetings, site visits, and event production responsibilities. Local travel throughout the DC region and national travel are required for site visits, installations, rehearsals, and live-event execution. Flexibility to work outside standard business hours, including occasional evenings and weekends, is required based on event schedules. Salary Range The anticipated salary range for this position is $100,000–$145,000 annually, commensurate with experience, qualifications, and fit with Precon’s needs. Why you will love working here You’ll play a meaningful role in shaping standout live experiences in the nation’s capital and beyond, joining a fun, entrepreneurial team that values creativity, collaboration, accountability, and continuous learning. You’ll have the opportunity to work directly with clients, influence the solutions we bring to the table, and collaborate with talented creative, technical, sales, and production professionals to turn ideas into experiences. This is a highly visible role with the opportunity to make a direct impact on both the work we produce and the client relationships that drive Precon’s growth. What You Bring to the Table 5+ years of relevant experience in live events, experiential marketing, event production, creative event strategy, or a closely related environment, with meaningful experience working directly with clients. A strong understanding of live-event production and how creative, scenic, technical, content, venue, and production considerations come together to create an effective audience experience. A consultative, client-facing approach. You listen well, ask thoughtful questions, uncover what a client is really trying to accomplish, and can help turn an early or incomplete idea into a compelling solution. Strong presentation and communication skills, with the confidence to recommend, explain, and sell an approach to clients and senior stakeholders. Creative and strategic problem-solving skills, balanced with enough production knowledge to understand what is feasible, what it will take, and when to bring in additional expertise. Working knowledge of event budgets, proposals, vendor pricing, scopes of work, and production considerations, with the ability to balance creative ambition with budget and execution realities. Comfortable remaining engaged after the work is won, including participating in key production milestones and working onsite at live events as appropriate. Organized and accountable, with the ability to manage opportunities and priorities without needing to personally project-manage every detail of event execution. Preferred experience includes: Experience working in a live-event production company, experiential agency, event agency, or similar client-service environment. Experience contributing to event concepts, pitches, proposals, or new-business presentations. Familiarity with renderings, design boards, site plans, stage/scenic concepts, room layouts, and other tools used to communicate live-event ideas. Sales, business development, or account-growth experience, particularly experience, helping turn qualified opportunities into awarded work. About Precon Events Precon Events is an industry leader in live event production, known for creating emotional, memorable experiences around the world. Our team of Producers, Technical Directors, Project Managers, and Event Gurus brings together world-class talent and cutting-edge technology to deliver exceptional events. We thrive under pressure and are committed to excellence in every facet of event planning and execution. The Perks (Because You Deserve Them) At Precon Events, we take care of our people. Our benefits include medical, dental, life, and both short- and long-term disability insurance, plus a 401(k) plan to help you plan for the future. We offer generous paid time off that grows into uncapped vacation after your first year, along with the flexibility of a fully remote workplace with no commute, just great work with great people. Please note that while we value flexibility, this role requires candidates to be based in the Washington, DC metro area. Only local applicants will be considered. An Inclusive Place to Do Your Best Work Precon Events is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants and team members of all backgrounds and identities. We’re committed to creating a workplace that’s free of discrimination, harassment, and anything that gets in the way of great work and good people.

input.description: Overview Of The Drum The Drum is transforming from a traditional publishing company into a global media, events and intelligence business that connects the world's marketing leaders through journalism, experiences, insights and community. The Role As the Editorial Coordinator, you will sit at the intersection of editorial, events, audience development and commercial strategy across the US market. This highly visible role is responsible for bringing together content, industry relationships and live experiences to create meaningful engagement opportunities for our audience, partners and contributors. You will work directly with editors, journalists, event producers, commercial leaders and industry stakeholders to shape content opportunities around major industry moments, coordinate high-profile interviews and speakers, and help maximize the impact of The Drum's events and editorial platforms. This role is ideal for a highly organized relationship-builder who thrives in fast-paced environments, enjoys connecting people and ideas, and wants to play an influential role in shaping conversations across the marketing, advertising and media industries. The Opportunity This is a highly visible, cross-functional role sitting at the intersection of content, events and industry engagement. You will drive coordination across The Drum's editorial and events ecosystem, helping to maximize opportunities around major industry moments, conferences, awards, speakers and brand partnerships. You will work closely with editors, journalists, event producers, commercial teams and industry stakeholders to ensure our content and event strategies are aligned and delivering maximum impact. The ideal candidate is highly organized, relationship-driven and commercially aware, with a passion for media, marketing and events. You thrive in fast-paced environments, enjoy bringing people and projects together, and can confidently manage multiple priorities while maintaining exceptional attention to detail. Key Responsibilities Editorial & Industry Content Coordination Own coordination of editorial activity surrounding major industry events, conferences, awards and key marketing moments. Manage interview schedules, speaker availability and editorial opportunities across content and event initiatives. Support the planning and execution of editorial projects tied to live experiences and industry engagement. Maintain and oversee editorial planning calendars related to events, conferences and industry activations. Identify opportunities to expand editorial coverage, thought leadership and audience engagement around key industry moments. Events & Editorial Integration Partner closely with editorial and events teams to ensure strong alignment between content strategy and event programming. Coordinate event-related content opportunities across editorial, video, social media and audience channels. Develop and manage workflows that maximize content capture before, during and after events. Identify and develop opportunities involving speakers, judges, contributors, sponsors and industry partners. Serve as a key liaison between editorial, events, commercial and marketing teams throughout planning and execution cycles. Speaker, Contributor & Industry Relationship Management Build and maintain relationships with contributors, speakers, judges, agency leaders, marketers and industry influencers. Coordinate outreach, scheduling and communication with high-profile industry stakeholders. Maintain contributor, speaker and industry contact databases and planning resources. Ensure a positive and professional experience for guests and contributors throughout editorial and event engagements. Support ongoing community-building efforts that strengthen The Drum's industry network and reputation. US Market Development & Industry Engagement Support The Drum's continued growth and visibility across the US marketing, advertising and media landscape. Research industry trends, conferences, networking opportunities and emerging sectors relevant to The Drum's audience. Identify key industry contacts, thought leaders and partnership opportunities that support editorial and commercial objectives. Coordinate US-based industry engagement activities and market-facing initiatives. Support event planning logistics, travel coordination and stakeholder management as required. Editorial Operations & Workflow Management Support editorial leadership with forward planning, content coordination and operational execution. Manage planning trackers, workflow systems and project documentation. Monitor project timelines and proactively follow up on deliverables and action items. Recommend and implement process improvements that enhance efficiency, collaboration and communication. Ensure seamless coordination across teams operating across multiple locations and time zones. High-profile speakers, contributors and industry leaders actively engage with The Drum's platforms. Content opportunities generated through events are effectively planned, captured and amplified. Cross-functional teams remain aligned on priorities, timelines and business objectives. The Drum continues to strengthen its presence, relationships and influence within the US marketing community. Requirements Qualifications & Experience Required 2-5 years of experience in media, publishing, conferences, events, content marketing, partnerships, community engagement or a related field. Exceptional organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously. Strong written and verbal communication skills. We only partner with inventive businesses that inspire us and continually challenge us to think big, but act small. Why bread & Butter: We are Southerners at heart, always saying, "Please" and "Thank You," and hustlers by trade. We believe everyone deserves a seat at the table and practice what we preach to ensure the spirit of hospitality runs through everything we do. We're not a company that wastes time—not yours, not ours. We are not too busy to talk, come by or think of new ways to increase long-term brand awareness. For us, there is little difference between work and pleasure because our work is our pleasure. We're Looking at You! A Digital Coordinator with Bread & Butter is a social media whiz kid, go-getter, and many-hat wearer who is ready to roll up your sleeves and get to work. You can't get enough social media, whether it's following the top influencers, keeping up with the latest Insta-trends or stepping up your Story game. You're also obsessed with restaurants, wine, food products, destinations, travels and hotels and most likely have been a waiter, front desk clerk, line cook or oenophile in a past life. You are the account dynamo, helping meet client goals by coordinating creative social media content, building relationships with influencers, engaging the online community, analyzing insights and consistently offering creative and on-point deliverables. A proverbial eager beaver, you meet or beat deadlines, stay ahead of trends and always look for a new way to skin a cat. You like to go big – because going home isn't an option (and duh, there's no wine at home). You're learning to be a problem solver and you value the relationships you're building via social. A Digital Coordinator for Bread & Butter should be thoughtful, creative, a strong writer, possess an almost obsessive attention to detail. You're the first to get in the mix when helping means the chance to learn more. Here's What We Need: New grads to 1 year of hospitality and/or travel social media experience, preferably with agency vs. in-house. Show us that you can post and create social media content for multiple brands. A passion for cultivating talent and helping our accounts grow. How can we be better? You have ideas. Knowledge of the latest influencers in the market and understanding how to create an influencer list for a campaign - you know who's on the pulse of pop culture, food, beverage and travel content. Experience shooting images and video with an eye on the latest content trends. Appreciates the art of dotting I's and crossing T's. The devil is in the details. Social media junkie- there's no such thing as reading/watching/engaging/posting too much. Bonus points for pop culture acumen and wicked photo skills. Leads accounts by example, showcasing professionalism, punctuality and problem solving while maintaining a sense of humor. Has the ability to really dig deep into client goals to help teams secure meaningful and impactful social media content. Enjoys helping teams create social media accounts that make others say "WOW. That's rad." Love of a fast-paced environment and the satisfaction of a busy yet productive day. Flexibility and a desire for endless possibilities. B&B is a dynamic, ever-evolving company that thinks beyond black and white. Excitement for growth, new ideas, new ways of doing things and a place you're excited to call home. Say yes! Working Conditions On the whole, this is a hybrid, office-based role. A Digital Coordinator will spend time in meetings and briefings. Occasional travel might be required for client visits and planning. This position is considered sedentary to light work, and employees are not required to lift or move heavy objects. Although a Coordinator's commitment will tend to be standard office hours, deadlines or the demands of a client may see the Coordinator working nights or weekends to ensure continued success. Must be authorized to work in the US. Having Our Cake & Eating it too: Generous paid time off Paid sick/personal time Birthday off (because who wants to work on their special day!) Endless summer Fridays (half-days year 'round baby) Flexible, hybrid schedule Work from any Bread & Butter office when you're in town Medical and dental + dependents Extended benefits (vision, life, disability, EAP) Generous maternity and family planning leave 3% contribution to 401k regardless of participation Cell phone reimbursement New business bonuses Employee referral bonus Weekly Wine Wednesdays (cheers with your local team!) Robust training program Mentorship program Local love (yearly giveback initiative) Compensation: The hourly range for this role is $22 to $24.

input.description: Outlier is an AI training platform owned and operated by Scale AI. Outlier Experts work on a variety of projects, from generating training data to evaluating the performance of models. About the opportunity: We are seeking detail-oriented English speakers to review AI-generated media. Roleplay live conversations with an AI voice model and score each exchange, compare generated images and videos to judge which follows the prompt better, and explain in writing what looked or sounded wrong, all remotely and on your own schedule. At Outlier, your expertise helps shape how advanced AI systems reason, learn, and improve. Through Outlier’s evaluation and feedback loop, your work helps turn frontier research into AI that performs better in the real world. Responsibilities: Holding a live, scenario-based conversation in English with AI voice models, then ranking how natural, useful, and clear each one sounded Comparing pairs of AI-generated images and videos and judging which one better follows the prompt Inspecting outputs closely, including zooming in and replaying, to spot problems like distorted anatomy, flickering or unnatural motion, text errors, and audio that doesn't match the video Rating each output across dimensions like adherence, quality, and realism, then writing a specific explanation in English that points to what you saw or heard Common tasks: Image evaluations: Compare two AI-generated images for the same text prompt and pick the better one, judging how well each follows the instructions, visual quality, and visible AI artifacts. Some tasks rank edited images against the original. Video evaluations: Rank AI-generated videos against a text prompt, or edited videos against their source clip. Video caption labeling: Label first-person videos of people or robots doing hands-on tasks. Contributors split each clip into individual actions and write precise captions, starting from an AI draft and correcting it. Audio and voice evaluations: Rate AI-generated speech on naturalness, pronunciation, and how closely it matches a target voice. Some tasks require recording a short voice explanation of the choice. Ideal qualifications: Fluent English speaker with strong, clear written communication and comfortable with natural, everyday conversational speech Strong attention to detail, with the patience to look and listen closely, and to replay or zoom in when something seems off Comfortable thinking on your feet and talking through realistic situations in a natural, conversational way Experience writing short, evidence-based explanations or reviews Comfortable making a clear decision when both options have flaws Nice to have: Pursuing or holding a Bachelor's degree or above What you'll need to sign up: A valid ID and mobile phone from your country of residence An up-to-date resume that highlights your expertise A LinkedIn profile showing your educational background and work experience Payment: Project work: Earn up to USD $15 per hour Additional incentives: On average, contributors earn an additional 7.5% through Missions — Outlier’s version of surge pricing. The top quartile boosts their earnings by an average of 11%. Payment schedule: Payments are processed weekly on Tuesdays, covering tasks completed during the previous pay period (Tuesday to Monday at midnight UTC), via PayPal, AirTM, or ACH transfer. Rates vary based on expertise, skills assessment, location, project need, and other factors. For example, higher rates may be offered to PhDs. For non-core work, such as during initial project onboarding or project overtime phases, lower rates apply. Additional incentives data is based on payments made in the past six months and is updated quarterly. Certain projects offer incentive payments. Please review the payment terms for each project. Why join Outlier: Work flexibly from anywhere, anytime, with no minimum hours. Set your own schedule, whether that's five or 40+ hours per week. Free access to leading LLMs, worth $200+/month Join 900K+ Outlier Experts across 52 countries, with $600M+ paid to experts Collaborate with experts in your field to push the boundaries of pre-release models How to apply: Create an account on Outlier Upload your resume Upload your valid ID Start earning by completing tasks Currently accepting applicants from: Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, United Kingdom, and United States. Please note: This is a 1099 contract opportunity on the Outlier.ai platform. You will join Outlier as a freelancer/independent contractor, not an employee. Because this is a freelance opportunity, we do not offer internships, sponsorship, or employment. You must be authorized to work in your country of residence. If you are an international student, you may be able to sign up for Outlier if you are on a visa. You should contact your tax and/or immigration advisor with specific questions regarding your circumstances.

input.description: About UsDorsia is at the forefront of hospitality-tech innovation, redefining how the world gains access to the most in-demand restaurants, events, and experiences. By fusing cutting-edge technology with the art of luxury hospitality, we empower our members to secure impossible-to-get reservations while providing operators with unprecedented levels of control, visibility, and revenue optimization. In 2025, we grew revenue 480% and scaled to 400+ venues across 25 destinations, with the launch of our Culture Calendar extending Dorsia beyond restaurants into the world's most sought-after cultural moments. Backed by $54M in funding from investors including Index Ventures, Invus, and Red Sea Ventures, and strategic partners including MoonPay, Major Food Group, and The Dinex Group / Daniel Boulud, we are entering our most consequential phase of growth and reshaping the global hospitality landscape. We're adding exceptional talent to drive what comes next. About the RoleDorsia is seeking a Video Editor to bring our editing in-house. This is a role for an editor with a real instinct for pacing and hooks, someone who can sit with hours of unscripted footage from a restaurant, an event, or a founder's trip and find the story inside it. You will cut across the full range of our output, from same-day social clips to polished restaurant short-form and longer-form documentary-style episodes. As we build recurring social franchises like our docu-series, you will help define what they look and feel like. We operate on the hospitality clock, our volume is high, and work goes live quickly. If you want to ship often and own formats, rather than sit inside a long-post pipeline, this role is for you. What You’ll DoEditing & StorytellingEdit across a wide range of formats, from fast-turn social clips to polished restaurant films and longer-form documentary-style episodes.Cut footage from events, travel, restaurants, office life, founder content, interviews, and behind-the-scenes moments into stories that hold attention.Turn long-form footage, interviews, and documentary material into short, highly watchable clips built for social.Work from large volumes of unscripted footage and shape it into a clear narrative.Bring a sharp instinct for pacing, hooks, music, and selects to every cut.Story & CraftFind the shot. Anticipate what the edit needs and capture the B-roll, coverage, and moments that let an editor tell the story.Shoot for both vertical and horizontal formats, with an instinct for what holds attention on social.Move fluidly between polished produced work and fast, rough-and-ready capture depending on what the moment calls for.Handle light editing and quick-turn assembly when speed matters more than a full post cycle.Format BuildingHelp build recurring formats including mini mic series, docu-style YouTube episodes, event coverage, and other social-first franchises.Move between rough-and-ready social content and more polished brand or partner work without losing the Dorsia voice.Create and apply captions, title cards, basic graphics, and simple on-screen treatments.Test ideas, learn from what performs, and bring that back into the next cut.Speed & CollaborationDeliver on rapid turnarounds, including same-day and next-day edits when the moment calls for it.Take clear creative direction and execute against it quickly.Work closely with our videographer, producers, social, and editorial teams from shoot planning through publish.Stay organized across footage, project files, versioning, and handoffs on multiple concurrent projects.The Winning Recipe2-5 years of professional editing experience, ideally in the 2-4 year range.Based in New York, NY or Miami, FL.A portfolio showing range across social-first content, brand work, and longer-form or documentary-style storytelling.Strong working knowledge of Premiere Pro. Familiarity with DaVinci Resolve and audio tools is a plus.Motion design experience is a bonus, not a requirement.Collaborative, low-ego, and comfortable working closely with producers, shooters, social, and editorial.Excited by a high-output environment where we are building new formats, testing ideas, and publishing frequently.Genuine interest in luxury, culture, hospitality, or premium consumer brands.Compensation: New York Pay Range $80,000 - $100,000USD Workplace Philosophy at DorsiaAt Dorsia, we believe that culture eats strategy. The best ideas in the world mean nothing without the right people around the table and the right chemistry between them. We are, unapologetically, a people-first organization. In-Person Matters We’re creating once-in-a-lifetime experiences for the most discerning audience in the world. That doesn’t happen over Zoom. It happens through collisions: a spark across a desk, a kitchen-side conversation that unlocks a partnership, the energy of ideas felt, not typed. That’s why in-office culture is non-negotiable at Dorsia. Who We Hire We don’t subscribe to check-the-box hiring. We hire for merit and mindset, which naturally creates a team with varied backgrounds. What unites us isn’t demographics, it’s a shared vision: to build the social operating system for the cultural vanguard. Lifestyle Hours We’re not a 9-to-5 company. Our lifestyle mirrors our members. Early flights, after-work events, and late-night sprints when the work demands it. But we love what we do, and we definitely love a good party. High Performance Culture Working at Dorsia isn’t for everyone—and that’s the point. Our culture is designed for builders, not passengers. We move fast, set ambitious standards, and expect people to rise to them. If you have the talent and the drive, this will be a ride to remember. A Final Word We’re building something special. It will take long hours and relentless effort. It’s not for everyone. For those with the metabolism, you’ll create something that changes how culture is lived. And that’s the kind of work worth your life’s energy. Skills: Adobe Premiere, Caption Writing, Chemistry, Consumer Branding, Demographics, Design Services, Documentaries, Editing, Funding, Graphics, Leading Edge Technology, Multitasking, Music, Operating Systems, Organizational Skills, Restaurant, Revenue Growth, Storytelling, Team Player, Testing, Video Editing, YouTube Dorsia

input.description: FAENA ROSE Faena Rose is an exclusive, art and culture-based private members club founded on the principles of art, culture, community, and access. Faena Rose brings together its dynamic community of like-minded innovators, entrepreneurs, industry leaders, artists, and cultural influencers through a year-round calendar of engaging and transformative cultural experiences. FAENA GROUP Founded in Argentina by Alan Faena, Faena Group is a pioneering business specializing in the creation of one-of-a-kind holistic environments anchored in cultural experiences and socially responsible projects, ranging from residences and hotels to art and cultural spaces. OVERVIEW Faena is a celebrated ultra-luxury experience and one of the most recognized names in hospitality and culture — Faena has already been named Best Hotel Instagram of the Year. Faena Rose upholds the same standard of taste. This role isn't for everyone. It's for someone with aligned visual expectations, real discipline, and a genuine point of view about what makes content worth watching — not someone chasing views. However, the KPI for this role is follower growth, and the right views are required. You'll work closely with our Creative Director to bring a defined content point of view to life — on time, on brand, to a high standard — while owning the moment-to-moment judgment calls that no strategy deck can anticipate. For the right person — someone who successfully runs daily execution end-to-end — this position has genuine potential to evolve into a lead creative role as our content operation scales. We're not filling a static job description; we're looking for someone to grow into this role as it evolves. This is a junior-level position today. What we need is drive, discipline, and taste: someone who wants to learn fast, execute daily, and grow into the role. This is an in-person role, based full-time at Faena in Miami Beach — in the office daily and on-site at the majority of events annually (80+ events). REPORTING STRUCTURE & KEY PARTNERSHIPS Reports to: General Manager or Marketing Manager (day-to-day creative direction from the Creative Director)Peer teams: Member Relations, Marketing, Event Production, Cultural ProgrammingDirect reports: N/AKey collaborators: Marketing Manager, reative Director, Cultural Programming Lead, outside photo/video vendors at large-scale events DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES On-Site Moment Capture Serve as the lead moment-capture person at Faena Rose events — the person always hunting for the unplanned moment, not just the shot list.Shoot confidently and independently with a gimbal-stabilized camera (DJI Osmo Pocket or similar), and be comfortable with D-log/flat color profiles for proper grading.Approach talent, speakers, and patrons for cold intros and candid reflections without hesitation, including in fast-moving, high-profile, not-always-easy-to-manage environments.Own the shot list at smaller events; direct and manage outside photo/video teams at larger ones.Deliver organized footage to editors immediately following each event. Editing & Content Production Edit short-form content (Reels, Shorts) in Adobe Premiere or equivalent.Design YouTube thumbnails, static posts, and carousels in Adobe, Canva, or Figma.Build basic graphics and GIFs for our newsletter and support newsletter creation and management.Write short-form copy that tells a story or surfaces an idea. Product marketing copy is not what we are looking for. We focus on storytelling and moments. Maintain brand-consistent templates for repeatable formats, using AI tools to extend capacity where useful. Publishing & Channel Management Own social media day-to-day in full: content calendar, publishing cadence, and scheduling across Instagram, YouTube, and LinkedIn.Post with correct captions, tags, metadata, and YouTube SEO (titles, descriptions, timestamps).Manage platform mechanics daily — comments, community response, scheduling tools.Run the production workflow in ClickUp: tasks, deadlines, approvals, handoffs.Own and continually improve our AI-assisted content workflows — identify where AI tools can extend output quality and speed, and keep pushing that forward.Track competitor and industry accounts, staying ahead of platform and algorithm shifts.Report weekly on performance (views, reach, engagement, subscriber growth) and platform/trend intelligence, giving management what they need to adjust social and broader marketing strategy in real time. SKILLS & ABILITIES A media production mindset first, a social media skill set second — you think in shots, story arcs, and moments, not in campaigns or CTAs.Real experience shooting vertical video of people at live events or in interview settings — not product or food content.Comfortable and self-possessed enough to walk up to talent or a high-profile guest and get the shot, unprompted.Working knowledge of gimbal operation and D-log or similar flat color profiles.Proficient in Adobe Premiere (or equivalent) for short-form editing, and in Adobe, Canva, or Figma for static and carousel design.Fluent in how content actually performs on Instagram and YouTube — algorithm behavior, format mechanics, what a scroll-stopping moment looks like — without needing to sell a product or widget anything to get there.Hyper-organized: you run on checklists and calendars, and deadlines are not suggestions.Attention to details on editing STRONG PREFERENCES Experience with ClickUp or a comparable project management tool — a major plus.Experience building and managing a newsletter — a major plus.YouTube SEO fluency: titles, descriptions, timestamps, chaptering.Color correction experience using LUTs and working in LOG formats — a bonus, not required.An eye that catches brand inconsistency before it ships.Comfortable taking strong creative direction from a Creative Director with a defined visual point of view and executing it faithfully. PROACTIVE COMMUNICATION This team moves fast and the work is interdependent. If something is unclear, delayed, or stuck, we need to know before it becomes a bigger problem — including if the bottleneck is leadership. You raise issues early, ask clarifying questions rather than guess, and are comfortable telling a senior leader “I need a decision on this to move forward.” QUALIFICATIONS 2-4 years of hands-on content creation experience (internships, freelance, or in-house with a camera in hand) — this is a junior role, and we're hiring for taste, discipline, and drive as much as résumé.A content portfolio demonstrating both graphic design and video editing work is required to be considered.Availability for evenings, weekends, and key event dates — this is an in-person role, on-site at Faena Rose events. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS Ability to move safely on uneven terrain or in confined spaces.Ability to identify and respond to potential hazards.Ability to remain stationary for extended periods.Ability to lift or carry up to 40 lbs. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS Medical, dental, and vision insurance.401(k) with employer match.Vacation and PTO package.Additional employee benefits.
